1. MAJOR findings

# Finding Status Evidence
M4-1 The fit card quoted the least pessimistic axis, so "Too big by 0 cm" was possible FIXED FitVerdict.kt:126 passes the overall verdict to limitingOf. limitingOf (:153-160) chooses only among axes whose verdict equals it: TOO_BIG takes min(c + z·σc), the largest overshoot; FITS takes min c, the smallest spare; TIGHT takes min(c − z·σc). The set is never empty, because the overall verdict is the worst axis verdict. PlaceVerdict.kt:104-109 quotes axes[limiting.itemAxis], which is correct under rotation. Tests that fail on the old code: FitVerdictLinearTest.tooBigQuotesTheAxisThatIsTooBigNotAWideTightOne (the reviewer's TV case: the old rule picks the height at −8.5 cm), fitsQuotesTheSmallestSpareEvenWhenAnotherAxisHasTheLowerMargin (the old rule picks H with 8 cm spare), and PlaceVerdictTest.mixedAxesQuoteTheAxisThatDecides, which checks the card amounts: 5 cm, rounded up, and 3 cm, rounded down.
M4-2 saveMesh required extents equal to the GLB box, so every real scan would have thrown FIXED Writer: GlbWriter.writeMesh(keepInputOrigin = true) (GlbWriter.kt:257-297) writes the positions unchanged, so the scan stays in the measured box frame. It requires the frame origin within ORIGIN_SLACK_M = 0.5 m of the mesh. Draft: MeshDraft (GalleryDrafts.kt:65-83) carries glbExtents, checked against the extras, and meshExtents, the §7.1.5 values. Save: saveMesh (GalleryRepository.kt:250-289) checks the kind and origin, checks matches(info, glbExtents) and the GLB bytes, then writes mesh_extent_* and the new mesh_glb_* columns. Placement: usable() (:603-617) checks a mesh against mesh_glb_*. End-to-end test: ScanSaveEndToEndTest.reconScanSavesAndPlacesAtItsMeasuredFootprint runs real TSDF fusion, then marching cubes, floor cut, largest component, decimation to 15k, MeshExtent, writeMesh, saveMesh and modelForPlacement. It asserts that the GLB box and the extents differ, that W/H/D are the measured box, that the bottom is at the floor cut, and that the footprint is centred at 0 ± 1 voxel. The last run printed "304380 B, 15000 tris; GLB 605.8 × 391.0 × 406.3 mm, extents 602.5 × 400.4 × 403.6 mm, bottom 10.0 mm". The old saveMesh rejects this draft. The contract is updated in phase0.md §1 and §5.
P1-1 AdMob initialised for Pro after a stale cache or reinstall plus slow Play FIXED Signal: EntitlementRepository.settled (EntitlementRepository.kt:113-121) becomes true in a finally after the first APP_START refresh, whether it is answered or failed (:150-155). Ads: AdsManager.start (AdsManager.kt:151-157) waits for settled, capped at SETTLE_WAIT_MS = 12 s (:406), which is above the 10 s connect timeout. Only then does it follow the entitlement, so the 1 s Free published from a stale cache is ignored. Wiring: MainActivity builds nothing billing- or ads-related before the first frame. It then calls container.onFirstFrame(), which starts the entitlement, followed by ads.start. Tests: AdsManagerProTest "stale cache – Free before Play answers is not trusted, then Pro" and "slow Play – Unknown for 5 s, then Pro" both expect zero consent requests and zero inits. Before the fix, the old test asserted the opposite. "Play never answers" checks the 12 s cap. Residual: if Play takes longer than 12 s, the ads follow the cache. That is accepted.
P1-2 Rolling the clock back inside the grace window gave unlimited offline Pro FIXED CachedEntitlement.lastSeenMillis is a persisted high-water mark (Entitlement.kt:56-60). seen() only moves it forward (:143-144), on every Failed query (:90). effective() (:130-140) returns Free when now < max(lastSeen, confirmedAt) − 5 min, and computes age as max(now, highWater) − confirmedAt. Tests: EntitlementReducerTest "rollback inside the grace window cannot extend it" (day 6 seen, clock set to day 1, Free), "repeated rollbacks never get past 7 days of observed time", and "small NTP correction below the high-water mark keeps Pro". The first fails on the old code. Residual (documented in the KDoc, :126-128): a user who sets the clock back before every launch, with the Play Store disabled throughout, still gets 7 days of app-observed time. That is inside ADR-004's client-only threat model.
P1-3 The paywall sold a 20-item gallery cap that nothing enforced FIXED GallerySaveGate (GallerySaveGate.kt:17-53) gives checkItem and checkDeviceScan. A count error lets the save through. The counts are COUNT(*) queries (GalleryDao), which load no rows. At scan entry, before AR: AppNavHost.kt:91-98 (Home and Gallery onScan) opens the paywall instead of the Scan route. At Save: AppNavHost.kt:140 wires ScanViewModel canSave, and ScanViewModel.kt:249-253 keeps the whole draft with galleryFull = true. GalleryFullCard then offers Upgrade, Share sizes, and Discard behind a confirmation. That card appears on Review, which is a non-AR step. Rule: ProCatalog.kt:106 keeps GALLERY_UNLIMITED shipped = true, and it is now true. Tests: GallerySaveGateTest (20th allowed, 21st needs Pro; a lapse blocks only the next save; the 3D cap sits inside the gallery cap; an unreadable count never blocks) and ScanViewModelTest.galleryFullKeepsTheDraftAndSavesAfterUpgrade.

3. Decisions on the open technical calls

(a) C5 ±: scale term rel·L, no height inflation. ACCEPTED, with condition R2.

The argument that settles it is the physics of the depth source:

  • RAW depth-from-motion is triangulated from the VIO poses.
  • A VIO scale error therefore scales the whole fused model consistently: camera positions, depths and surfaces together.
  • So the error on an extent is rel·L, not rel·r̄.

The old max(L, √2·r̄) modelled something else: an independent depth-scale bias. Such a bias moves each observed face along its viewing ray by about bias·r̄. That is a different error, and it applies mainly to hardware ToF depth and to per-device depth calibration.

Applying the old term to depth-from-motion made the ± 3–6× the error. The H ±95 was 38.6 mm against a p95 error of 6.2 mm. That is uninformative, and review MINOR 10 rightly asks the tests to reject it.

Evidence:

  • The revised ± covers 200/200 seeded trials on every axis, at 2.25× (W), 3.07× (H) and 2.68× (D) the p95 error.
  • The trials include a uniform ±1.5% scale error.
  • The new upper-bound assertion (≤ 4× p95) passes, and it would have failed under the old formula.

Dropping height inflation is consistent with the source. Research §7.6 places the silhouette inflation on W and D, and H is measured from the support plane.

Why the residual risk is tolerable:

  • The mesh extents are never the item's size (ADR-013). They feed only the "3D shape (approximate)" line and the cross-check.
  • The cross-check tolerance is floored at max(3 cm, 3%). For objects under about 1 m, a slightly narrow mesh ± barely changes the badge. Where it does, it errs towards ROUGH, which is a warning and the honest direction.

What the synthetic tests cannot show is whether real depth has a range-dependent bias. Spike exit criterion 1 (§7.1.10) scans the carton at one distance only, so it cannot separate rel·L from bias·r̄. → R2: add a two-range check to the spike. If the error grows with range at fixed L beyond the ±, restore a range term for that DepthSource (for example rangeBiasRel · r̄, set per source) before the mesh ± is shown to users.

(b) Rejection of the prepaid 31-day cut-off (P1 MINOR 4). UPHELD.

Builder B is right.

  • The client cannot tell the two cases apart. Play's Purchase does not expose the base plan, so the client cannot distinguish a prepaid pass30 from a cancelled yearly. Both report autoRenewing = false.
  • The cut-off would revoke paying users. A cancelled yearly plan legitimately stays active for up to a year after purchaseTime, so the cut-off would take paid Pro away from cancelled-yearly users. That is a refund risk and a Play policy risk, and the users are honest ones.
  • The benefit is small. The legitimate path already revokes: Play stops returning an expired pass, and the next Ok query means Free. The cut-off would only stop replay through a fake billing service. That attack needs a rooted or hooked Play environment, which is already inside ADR-004's accepted threat model ("a patched APK skips the check").

ADR-004 now records "Replay of a genuine purchase" and "Expired prepaid passes" as accepted residual risks. purchaseTime is carried in OwnedPurchase for the server check. The real fix is server verification through the Play Developer API, and §8.3 already makes that a release gate before anything with marginal cost, such as cloud credits, ships.

4. New issues (introduced or exposed by the fix rounds)

None is a BLOCKER or MAJOR.

# Severity Where Problem and scenario Fix
N1 MINOR PlacementCore.kt:128-130, 296, 377-379 Problem: floorY is the minimum of every horizontal reticle hit in the session, point and depth hits included, and it never recovers. Scenario: a polished vitrified or marble floor (common in Indian homes) or a glass table can give one mirrored feature point a few cm below the real floor. Every genuine wall–floor tap is then more than MAX_OFF_FLOOR_M = 3 cm above floorY and gets rejected, and the eye-level readout reads high. Take floorY from tracked horizontal ARCore Planes only (the lowest plane), or from a robust low percentile of hits, never a single point. Add a test with one outlier below the floor. Device item 4.
N2 MINOR GallerySaveGate.checkItem → EntitlementFeatureGate.check, EntitlementRepository.kt:138-142 Problem: the gates wait only for "not Unknown", while the repository publishes Free from a stale cache at 1 s. MAJOR 1 fixed this for ads, not for gates. Scenario: a yearly Pro user with 25 items opens the app after 8 days and taps "Scan object" within about 1–3 s. They see the paywall. Nothing is lost: the paywall's refresh shows Pro, and Back works. In GallerySaveGate, when the answer is NeedsPro and settled is false, wait for settled (capped at about 5 s, with progress on the Scan button), then check again.
N3 MINOR (before D) PlacementMath.kt:35-36, 109-113; GlbWriter.writeMesh(keepInputOrigin) Problem: PlacedItem.centre assumes the GLB's bounding box is centred on its declared origin. A keepInputOrigin mesh breaks that by the 1 cm floor cut plus any asymmetry in a partial scan, up to ORIGIN_SLACK_M = 0.5 m. Scenario: floor placement is correct, because the offset is 0 there. A mesh switched to a wall target, or the wall centre-height readout, is off by that asymmetry. Write the bounding-box centre into the mesh extras (for example aabbCx, aabbCy, aabbCz via MeshExtras.values) and use it in PlacedItem, or restrict meshes to floor and table targets. Decide before D integrates.
N4 MINOR AppNavHost.kt:91-98 Problem: startScan navigates after a suspending check (≤ 1 s wait plus a count) without checking that the user is still on Home or Gallery. Scenario: tap Scan, then Settings within a second, and the Scan route opens on top of Settings. Before navigating, check navController.currentBackStackEntry is the entry that started the check.
N5 MINOR (perf) PlacementController.onFrame → toEngine() (SessionSetup.kt:94), placedPose/modelPose, Placed.copy, NodeHolder.show (PlaceScreen.kt:249-250) Problem: about 15–25 small objects are still allocated per frame: ARCore pose plus engine Pose/Vec3/Quaternion per conversion, the state copy, and Float3/Quaternion for the node. That is roughly 30–60 KB/s at 30–60 Hz. MINOR 13 removed only the status snapshot. Profile at the 30 fps gate (device item 12). If GC shows in the trace, reuse mutable poses for the camera and anchor, and set the node transform from reused Float3/Quaternion.
N6 DOC GalleryRepository.kt:565 (KDoc of modelForPlacement) Says a mismatched mesh is "extras vs the mesh_extent_* columns". Since MAJOR 2 it is mesh_glb_*. A D builder reading the KDoc would compare against the wrong columns. One-line KDoc fix → R1.
N7 MINOR (lint) strings_pro.xml:10, 11, 13, 110 4 PluralsCandidate warnings. The counts are constants (20, 3, 2), so English and Hindi are correct today. There is also one UnusedResources (home_accuracy_good) and one UseKtx. Use <plurals> or tools:ignore="PluralsCandidate", and remove the unused string at the M6 lint pass.

Areas I checked in particular and found clean:

  • Threading:
    • EntitlementRepository mutates its sets and cache under one Mutex on Main. The 1 s timeout path reads only the @Volatile cache.
    • AdsManager is main-only.
    • GalleryRepository counts run on IO.
    • Mesh thumbnail encoding runs on cpu, and every catch rethrows CancellationException.
  • Cancellation:
    • commitLocked honours cancellation until the files are committed, then completes under NonCancellable. This is unchanged, and it now also covers templates and meshes.
    • The canSave false path returns before any write.
    • purchase() cancels its waiter when the launch fails.
  • Process death:
    • Place restores the target, spin, height and space, with a note.
    • galleryFull is not saved. It doesn't need to be: Scan restores to Outline, as in M3, and a second Save re-checks.
    • The entitlement cache and high-water mark are persisted on every change.
  • Seams: both builders' columns and counts, the MeshDraft fields and the end-to-end test agree. Place uses the row's W/H/D for the verdict and the GLB's extras for rendering, as K4 says.
  • Strings and lint: Hindi is complete (above). lintDebug reports app 0 errors / 6 warnings, and ar and data "No issues found".

7. Device-checklist items for docs/TESTING.md §18 (Place + 3D core)

Upgrade and data

  1. v2 → v3 upgrade (mandatory first): install the M4 APK over M3 on a phone with several gallery items (TV, frame, box) and History rows.
    • Every item still opens, shares and deletes, and History is intact.
    • Placing each M3 item once regenerates its model, which happens silently. The item still opens after an app restart.

Place

  1. True scale:
    • Place a gallery item next to the real object, or a box you scanned next to the box itself. The outline matches within the item's ±.
    • The "1:1 True size" chip is shown, and pinching never scales.
  2. Surfaces:
    • Floor, table and wall.
    • A frame or TV hangs flush and upright. A box stands on its bottom.
    • Move, rotate (90° and twist) and 1 cm nudges behave from several viewing angles.
  3. Plain wall fallback:
    • On a plain painted wall the fallback is offered after about 5 s. Two taps on the wall–floor line build the wall.
    • Two taps on a table edge are rejected.
    • Repeat on a polished vitrified or marble tile floor (N1). Note any wrongly rejected floor taps.
  4. Eye level and slider: the centre-height readout matches a tape within about 2 cm. The slider value survives "Don't keep activities".
  5. Fit verdict:
    • Measure a gap about 3 cm wider than a measured item: the card reads Tight (linear band).
    • Measure a gap 10 cm wider: Fits, quoting the smallest spare.
    • A wall rectangle where only the width is too small: "Too big by X · width" (M4 MAJOR 1).
    • A typed size shows "using your typed size".
  6. A floor rectangle shows "Height not checked".
  7. Pause and process death:
    • Power button on Place: the item is picked up, and the space is labelled "measured before the pause".
    • Under "Don't keep activities", the target, spin, height and space are restored with the restore note.
  8. Errors: delete the item while Place is open, in another task or via Back stack tricks. The screen says "deleted" and goes back, with no crash.
  9. Rendering: the photo face of a placed TV or frame matches the real colours (it is unlit). The sides are lit and not black.
  10. Ads:
    • Saved → Place → Back → item → Back: no ad anywhere.
    • Gallery item → Place → Back: no ad.
    • Never an ad over the camera.
  11. 30 fps: run gfxinfo on Place with a textured item placed, on the low-end and the mid-range phone. Frame time p95 must be ≤ 33 ms. Note any GC pauses in a trace (N5).
  12. Hindi and TalkBack: the Place screens in Hindi with nothing truncated. TalkBack reads the verdict card in full: verdict, amount, axis and notes.

3D core (spike, D milestone; depth phone)

  1. Carton 60×40×40 cm at about 0.7 m and about 1.5 m, 5 scans each. Record the mesh-extent error against a tape and the ± (decision (a), R2).
  2. If a ToF phone is available, repeat item 14 with ToF depth. If not, record the depth source the phone used.
  3. Memory, thermal and time:
    • 90 s capture from a cool start: peak extra PSS ≤ 40 MB (dumpsys meminfo).
    • No SEVERE thermal state.
    • Sofa processing ≤ 5 s.
  4. Sofa about 5 cm from a wall: no wall patch in the mesh, and D is not inflated (M4 MINOR 8).
  5. Saved scan:
    • The item is ≤ 0.5 MB (Settings storage, or the app's files).
    • It places standing on the floor at its measured footprint (bottom about 1 cm up).
    • The Gallery shows "Approximate 3D shape · measured size".
  6. Free caps: with 3 saved 3D scans on Free, the next 3D scan opens the paywall before the camera. The 20-item cap behaves as in TESTING §17 items 8–10.

8. Recommendations for the next phase

D: 3D-scan device spike, then app integration

  1. Spike first, with hard exits (§7.1.10) plus R2's two-range check. Run it on the user's depth phone with a release build. Do not write the D screens until items 1–4 pass, or until the Beta / "ToF and raw depth only" fallback has been decided.
  2. Pipeline order exactly as in ReconMemoryTest:
    • compute DepthNoise and the mesh_info numbers from the volume;
    • run marching cubes and release the volume;
    • then floor clip, keepLargestComponent(insideBox), decimation to 15k, MeshExtent, and finally writeMesh(keepInputOrigin = true). Copy the order from the test, not from memory.
  3. Budget handling at Save: if saveMesh throws on the byte check, decimate again to about 12k and retry once, then fall back to "Save as box". Never show a raw IllegalArgumentException.
  4. One gated insert path: add a GatedGalleryStore in :app that calls gallerySaveGate.checkDeviceScan() before saveMesh and keeps the draft on NeedsPro, like canSave. Gate DEVICE_SCAN before capture as well (K1), never mid-session.
  5. Settle the counting rule. countDeviceScans counts saved MESH_DEVICE rows, so deleting a scan frees a Free slot. The user decision was "3 free". Decide whether that means 3 saved at a time (as built) or 3 lifetime (needs a persisted counter), and say it on the paywall.
  6. Fix N3 (the mesh bounding-box centre in the extras) before meshes can target walls.
  7. K2 for D: saving a 3D scan does count as a completed scan. The after-save chance is used only by the next non-AR screen. Extend MeasureVisitTrackerTest.
  8. Process death and pause as in §7.1.6: no TSDF checkpoint, "Finish with what was captured" or "Start again", and "Save as box instead" from the kept numbers. Test each restore path in a ScanViewModel-style JVM test.
  9. Label everywhere: "Approximate 3D shape · measured size". Ship it as Experimental / Beta per PLAN §9's fallback rule until the bench shows the ± holds on real depth.

T: furniture templates

  1. Fix the rule conflict before building. ProCatalog gives FURNITURE_TEMPLATES free = None, but FREE_TEMPLATE_IDS says the sofa, bed and wardrobe templates are free. Model this as an allowance per template id (or a separate "core templates" feature). Flip shipped in the same change.

  4. Parts must union to exactly W×H×D (saveTemplate refuses otherwise, at 0.1 mm). Generate the parts from the measured W/H/D with closed-form maths, and property-test the union box over the parameter ranges.
  5. The verdict uses the bounding box (boundingBox = true for FURNITURE) for L-sofas. Say so on the card ("overall box"). A footprint-aware verdict is a later item.
  6. Budget: about 1 KB per part, so it is negligible. Keep MAX_PARTS = 512.

Reviewsdocs/reviews/M4-review.md · updated 16 Nov 2026, 11:33

M4 review: Phase 0 + M4 Place in room (Builder A) and engine/recon (Builder C)

Reviewer: Reviewer agent, 2026-11-06. Scope: the uncommitted work against 4f8ec1f (git status, git diff HEAD), limited to the files in the brief. Builder B's Pro, billing and ads code is out of scope, except where A uses K1, K2 and K5. Standard: FRIDAY §1 and §4.B, both the standard pass and the thermonuclear structural pass. Source was not edited, and Gradle was not run (the orchestrator reports the full build green: engine 249, ar 104, data 63, app 217).

Verdict: 0 BLOCKER, 2 MAJOR, 11 MINOR.

The core of M4 is sound:

  • The verdict combines uncertainties linearly by default, and its boundaries are tested.
  • The GLB contract (K8, ADR-003) is implemented as written. The photo face is unlit. The node is placed at 1:1 with scaleToUnits = null and centerOrigin = null.
  • The MeasureSession pooling removed the per-frame allocations it targeted, without aliasing.
  • Room v3 matches 3.json.
  • modelForPlacement regenerates through the existing atomic path and never touches a mesh.
  • Recon is deterministic, allocation-free in integrate, and its marching-cubes table is crack-free by construction.

The two MAJORs are both about what a number tells the user:

  1. The fit card can quote the wrong axis and amount on a "Too big" or "Fits".
  2. The open 1 cm GLB-versus-MeshExtent question is now a hard seam failure. As written, saveMesh would reject every real 3D scan.

How the findings were checked

  • Order (FRIDAY §4.B): I read the tests first, then the diff, then the call sites.
  • Fit verdict: checked by hand against FitVerdict.evaluate (engine/.../FitVerdict.kt:108-153), including the ranking expression and limitingAxis.
  • Room v3: I parsed data/schemas/.../3.json with Python and compared every new column (type, NOT NULL, default) with V3_STATEMENTS. All 12 statements match, and model_kind is TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PROXY_BOX' in both.
  • Strings: I diffed the keys of values/strings_place.xml and values-hi/strings_place.xml with a script: 66 and 66, none missing. Every R.string.place_* used in PlaceScreen.kt is defined. The %1$s / %1$d placeholders agree in both languages.
  • Decimator failure: I read the latest result file, engine/build/test-results/test/TEST-...VertexClusterDecimatorTest.xml (11:17Z = 16:47 IST, 4/4 passed), and the recon file timestamps (ls --time-style=full-iso).
  • Memory figures: computed from the LongIntMap sizing rule (VertexClusterDecimator.kt:243-245) and the sofa sizes that the test result file prints (133,588 → 19,898 triangles).

BLOCKER

None.

MAJOR

  1. The fit card quotes the axis with the least pessimistic margin, not the axis that decided the verdict. "Too big by 0 cm" is possible. engine/.../FitVerdict.kt:123-125, consumed at app/.../place/PlaceVerdict.kt:102-107 and PlaceScreen.kt:475-477.

    • Problem:
      • limiting = axes.minBy { c − z·σc } is taken over all axes, while fit = max(ordinal) (the worst verdict).
      • On a two-axis wall rectangle, a TIGHT axis with a wide band can have a lower c − band than the TOO_BIG axis.
      • The card then prints "Too big by |c|" using the TIGHT axis's clearance and names that axis.
      • The FITS variant overstates the spare. Take W at 3 cm spare with a 0.5 cm band (score 2.5) and H at 8 cm spare with a 6 cm band (score 2). The card says "Fits, 8 cm spare" on the height, while the width has only 3 cm.
    • Scenario:
      • A TV of 120 × 70 cm, measured with ± 0.5 cm, and FitRotation.NONE.
      • The wall space is measured as 115 ± 1 cm wide and 70 ± 8 cm tall (a long vertical edge measured from far away).
      • Width: c = −5 cm, band 1.5 cm, so TOO_BIG. Its score (c − band) is −6.5 cm.
      • Height: c = 0, band 8.5 cm, so TIGHT. Its score is −8.5 cm, which is lower.
      • Height therefore becomes limitingAxis, and the card reads "Too big by 0 cm · height" while the width is 5 cm over.
      • PlaceVerdictTest has no case with mixed per-axis verdicts.
    • Fix:
      • Choose the limiting axis among the axes whose verdict equals the overall verdict.
      • For TOO_BIG, take the largest overshoot (min c + band). For FITS, take the smallest clearance (min c). For TIGHT, keep the current rule.
      • This is one line in FitVerdict.evaluate (the doc comment already says limitingAxis is "what the UI quotes"), plus a mixed-axis test in FitVerdictLinearTest and PlaceVerdictTest.
    • If skipped: the headline verdict stays right, but the number and axis the user acts on ("by how much", "which side") can be wrong. That defeats R1's honesty goal on exactly the near-boundary cases it exists for.

  2. K10/K11 seam: saveMesh requires the mesh extents to equal the GLB's own bounding box, but §7.1.5 MeshExtent.estimate produces different numbers. As written, every real 3D-scan save throws. This is the open "1 cm heightM" item. data/.../GalleryRepository.kt:241; engine/.../GlbWriter.kt:269 (recentre); engine/.../recon/MeshExtent.kt:97-99.

    • Problem:
      • writeMesh re-centres on the mesh's own AABB, so extras.heightM = max_y − min_y. After the C2 floor clip, min_y is plane + max(1 cm, v).
      • MeshExtent.estimate measures H from the support plane (y = 0) to the 99.5th percentile, and W and D as 0.5–99.5 percentile spreads.
      • MeshExtents documents itself as "the mesh's own extents and ±, §7.1.5", and saveMesh demands matches(info, e.widthM, e.heightM, e.depthM) to 0.1 mm.
      • The ± stored beside these extents belongs to the percentile extents, not to the AABB.
    • Scenario:
      • Take the ReconSceneTest pipeline for the 60 × 40 × 40 cm box.
      • MeshExtent H is about 0.400 m, while the GLB heightM is about 0.390 m (the clip is at 1 cm). W and D differ by the percentile trim.
      • The D-milestone scan screen fills MeshExtents from Extent3, and require throws IllegalArgumentException, so the scan cannot be saved.
      • If a builder "fixes" it by passing the GLB extras instead, the mesh_extent_* columns hold AABB values with a ± computed for different quantities. The "3D shape: … ± 3" line is then inconsistent.
      • Placement also drops the mesh 1 cm and centres it on its own AABB (a partial scan is shifted sideways).
      • No test builds a MeshDraft from the real recon pipeline. GalleryPlacementTest uses hand-made meshes whose extents equal their AABB.
    • Fix (decide before the D milestone; the cheapest consistent option):
      • MeshDraft carries two things: glbExtents (checked against the extras, which keeps K8 "extras = own geometry") and meshExtents (the §7.1.5 values with ±, stored in the columns).
      • Add a writeMesh option to keep the input frame (origin = the box base, not the AABB's bottom centre), so a placed scan sits on the floor at its measured footprint.
      • Record the decision in phase0.md §5 and §7.1.4, and add one end-to-end test: fusedBox → writeMesh → saveMesh → modelForPlacement.
    • If skipped: the 3D scan's Save fails on first integration, or it stores self-inconsistent numbers.

MINOR

  1. A floor rectangle never checks height, and the card does not say so. PlaceVerdict.kt:95-98, 109.

    • Problem: heightNotChecked is set only for GAP. A floor AREA compares W × D only.
    • Scenario: a fridge in a niche under a cabinet. The user measures the floor rectangle, and the card reads "Fits, 3 cm spare" with no "height not checked" note, although the niche is 5 cm too low.
    • Fix: set heightNotChecked = space.kind == GAP || !onWall and word the note "Height not checked".

  2. The wall-fallback "on the floor" test is only relative to the first tap. ar/.../PlacementCore.kt:273-274.

    • Problem: the floor plane is built through tap a itself, so verticalThroughFloorLine's 3 cm off-floor check only compares b with a. The tilt check is trivially true.
    • Scenario: both taps land on the front edge of a 45 cm-high coffee table. A "wall" is built along the table edge, and a frame is hung on it. floorY (the lowest horizontal hit) is known and ignored.
    • Fix: when floorY is known, build the floor plane at floorY and reject taps more than MAX_OFF_FLOOR_M from it. Add a test with two points at the same raised height.

  3. A storage failure or an unreadable row on Place says "This item was deleted". GalleryRepository.modelForPlacement (:548) and guardedOrNull (:792-798) turn every exception into null, and PlaceViewModel maps null to PlaceLoad.Deleted.

    • Scenario: the disk is full during the one-time regeneration of an M3 model (glbVersion 1). The user is told their item was deleted. §3.6 requires the error card with Back.
    • Fix: return a sealed result (Missing | Failed | Ready), or rethrow IOException so the view model shows Failed.

  4. Spec drift in Place restore. PlaceViewModel.kt, PlaceScreen.kt.

    • Problem:
      • §3.4 and §3.6 specify a centre-height slider saved in SavedStateHandle, plus a space shown as "measured before the pause".
      • The build has only an eye-level button, does not save the height, and has no "before the pause" note.
      • After a pause the old space silently feeds the verdict for a re-placed item, which is acceptable (it is a length) but unlabelled.
    • Fix: implement the slider and its saved key and add the label, or amend §3.4 and §3.6.

  5. The marching-cubes saturation skip is dead code after C1. engine/.../recon/MarchingCubes.kt:46, 109, 112.

    • Problem:
      • With behindFraction = 0.5, integration never writes a TSDF value below −0.5 (TsdfVolume.kt:237-238).
      • A cube with any inside corner therefore always has a corner with |tsdf| < 0.9, so allSaturated is true only for all-positive cubes, which cfg == 0 already skips.
      • The rule the doc describes ("two truncated bands meeting") can no longer fire. The only test, unobservedAndSaturatedCubesAreSkipped, writes ±1 by hand with setVoxel, a value integration cannot produce.
    • Scenario: a chair rail or table edge thinner than about 6 cm is carved from both sides. The spurious crossing between −0.5 and +1 is not filtered, contrary to the §7.1.4 text.
    • Fix: scale the threshold to the asymmetric band (negative at −0.9 × behindFraction), or drop the rule and the doc claim.

  6. C6 keeps wall fragments, contrary to the doc. MeshSegmenter.kt:105-109 and §7.1.4 step 3.

    • Problem: the doc says "floaters and wall fragments go", but the 5 % rule keeps any piece with at least 5 % of the largest piece's area.
    • Scenario:
      • A 2.2 × 0.9 × 1.0 m sofa stands 5 cm from a wall, with the default 10 cm margin.
      • The wall patch inside the volume is about (2.2 + 0.2) × (0.9 + 0.1) ≈ 2.4 m², roughly 30 % of the sofa's surface. It is kept.
      • The GLB bounding box, MeshExtent D and the cross-check all include it, so the scan reads ROUGH or too deep.
      • The only test drops a 3 cm cube.
    • Fix: after C2, drop components that touch the volume's outer margin (outside the measured box), or fix the doc and rely on the crop step. Add a sofa-near-a-wall scene test.

  7. The decimator's working set is about 21 MB for the sofa, against a §7.1.6 estimate of "≤ ~10 MB", while the 12.6 MB TSDF is still alive. VertexClusterDecimator.kt:82-83, 135, and the pipeline order in §7.1.4.

    • Problem: each LongIntMap(n) takes the next power of two ≥ 2n + 2 slots at 12 B each. For the 133,588-triangle sofa:
      • edgeUse(3T) takes 1,048,576 slots, about 12.6 MB.
      • triMap(T) takes 524,288 slots, about 6.3 MB.
      • cellMap(V) takes about 3 MB.
      • The pipeline keeps the volume until DepthNoise.from(vol), which comes after decimation, so the peak is about 12.6 + 21 + the meshes, roughly 40 MB.
    • Scenario: a noisy real capture produces about 2× the synthetic triangle count. The spike's "peak extra PSS ≤ 40 MB" criterion (§7.1.10 item 3) fails on memory the algorithm doesn't need.
    • Fix:
      • Compute DepthNoise and observedFraction before meshing, then release the volume.
      • Size edgeUse by about 1.5T (a closed-ish mesh has E ≈ 1.5T).
      • Record the real figures in §7.1.6.

  8. Recon test quality: some assertions could pass with a wrong implementation, and others have thin margins. ReconSceneTest.kt:167, MeshProcessingTest.kt:156-162, 182.

    • Coverage test: it asserts only "≥ 95 % covered". A ± inflated tenfold passes, and the doc already reports a ± about 3.7× the worst error. Add an upper bound, for example mean ±95 ≤ 4 × the 95th-percentile error, so an over-wide ± fails.
    • Hausdorff test, original → decimated direction: "≤ cell·√3" is not guaranteed by construction. A cluster whose triangles all collapse has no output vertex (outId < 0), so its original vertices may be further away. It passes today with fixed seeds, but an upstream change to the fused mesh can flip it (see the decimator note below).
    • Sofa bounding-box check: it asserts ≤ 5 mm, and §7.1.4 reports "≤ 5 mm" measured. The margin is unknown. Print it, as the box test does.

  9. The template regeneration source is not wired. app/.../AppContainer.kt:48 calls GalleryRepository.create(appContext) without templates = …, although phase0.md §5 says the orchestrator wires Builder B's registry there.

    • Scenario: once templates are saved, any future GLB_VERSION bump, or a missing template file, makes Place show the plain measured box with no furniture shape, silently.
    • Fix: pass B's registry as a TemplateModelSource when it lands, and add a test in AppContainer (or a TODO tied to the T milestone).

  10. The origin → box-centre rule is implemented three times. GlbWriter.anchorOffset (GlbWriter.kt:323-327), PlacementMath.attachOffset (PlacementMath.kt:106-114) and PlacementCore.centreHeight (PlacementCore.kt:359-363).

    • Scenario: a fourth BoxOrigin (for example TOP_CENTER for pendant lamps) is added to the writer only. Placement then hangs items offset by half their size, and the eye-level readout is wrong.
    • Fix: have one owner in :engine (for example BoxOrigin.centreOffset(w, h, d): Vec3) and use it from all three places.

  11. Small per-frame allocations remain in the Place loop. PlacementController.kt:87-94, 208; PlacementCore.kt:88-97.

    • Problem: per frame there is a PlacementStatus data object (built even when the publish is throttled), two KClass references from state::class, SurfaceHit, and three or four Pose/Vec3/Quaternion values.
    • Scenario: at 30–60 Hz this is a steady garbage stream in exactly the loop the M4 30 fps gate profiles. It is small next to the remaining HitSample and ViewProjection allocations, and that is why this is MINOR.
    • Fix: compare state kinds with is checks, and build the status only when publishing.

The VertexClusterDecimatorTest failure (Builder A's run)

Read: it is not flaky by construction. The most likely cause is a mixed working-tree snapshot.

Why the code is deterministic:

  • Data structures: no HashMap or HashSet and no iteration in identity-hash order. LongIntMap is open addressing with fixed Fibonacci hashing, and clusters are numbered in vertex order.
  • Inputs and threading: all randomness is seeded (Random(0), Random(3)), and everything runs on a single thread.
  • Shared state: recon has no mutable global state (McTable is immutable after class init). JUnit 4 builds a new test-class instance per test, so fused by lazy is not shared. Gradle runs the classes sequentially in one worker.
  • Floating point: this is IEEE-strict Kotlin/JVM, with no automatic FMA, so the same inputs give the same bits.
  • sofaSizeMeshDecimatesTo20kAndIsDeterministic itself asserts bit-identical repeat output, and it passed.

Why a mixed snapshot is the likely cause:

  • The builders share one working tree. Builder C edited recon between 16:14 and 16:40:
    • TsdfVolume.kt at 16:14
    • VertexClusterDecimator.kt and TsdfVolumeTest.kt at 16:24:43
    • MeshSegmenter.kt and MeshProcessingTest.kt at 16:28
    • MarchingCubes.kt and its test at 16:40
  • A run started in that window could compile a new decimator against an old test (or an old fused mesh against new thresholds).
  • The latest result (16:47) passes 4/4 with margin: bounding-box change 1.77 mm against 5 mm, and 19,898 against 20,000 triangles.

Residual risk: the assertions in MINOR 10 (the unguaranteed Hausdorff direction and the unknown sofa margin) are where a legitimate upstream change, such as tuning C1 or C3, would show up as a "random" failure.

Recommendation: if it recurs on a clean tree, keep the XML (with system-out), because the printed per-bound deltas show which assertion moved.

Checked and OK

  • R1 and D6:
    • FitPolicy.combination defaults to LINEAR, and RSS is explicit opt-in.
    • The boundaries are tested at ± 0.1 mm, with a typed side, a frame turned portrait/landscape, a floor item turned W↔D, and minClearance.
    • The R1 sofa reads TIGHT.
    • Item σ is the rounded-up stored bound95 / 1.96, and typed or preset sides have σ = 0 and are labelled.
    • Amounts round cautiously: spare down, overshoot and band up, in whole cm or inches.
    • TV is NONE, frame is ANY, and a floor rectangle is ANY.
  • K8 and ADR-003:
    • Writer: extras carry W/H/D (the GLB's own bounding box), origin, glbVersion = 2 and modelKind. The geometry is translated, never scaled. KHR_materials_unlit is in extensionsUsed and on the textured front only, and the sides stay lit.
    • Mesh output: u16 indices only when V ≤ 65,535, so index 65,535 never occurs. COLOR_0 is RGBA8 normalised.
    • Reader: GlbReader reads only the header and the JSON chunk, never throws, and its number grammar accepts the writer's 1.0E-4 form.
  • True scale:
    • PlacedModel passes scaleToUnits = null and centerOrigin = null, editing is off, and NodeHolder never touches scale.
    • BOTTOM_CENTER on the floor puts the origin at the hit. BACK_CENTER on a wall is flush (back face at distance 0), as are BACK_CENTER on a table and BOTTOM_CENTER on a wall (checked by hand through attachOffset).
    • The placed pose is recomputed every frame from the anchor plus a local offset, so it neither drifts nor accumulates.
  • R3 pooling (MeasureSession):
    • Samples come from an 8-slot ArrayBlockingQueue.
    • A sample dropped by DROP_OLDEST returns through onUndeliveredElement. A failed trySend (closed channel, where no undelivered callback runs) is offered back exactly once.
    • The worker returns each sample in finally, after its last read. LocalSurfaceModel.addPoints copies the cloud, and Reading does not retain the endpoint list, so no pooled buffer escapes a frame.
    • Queue offer and poll give the happens-before edge between main and the worker.
    • latestCentreHit is reset at the start of each frame. The dispatcher calls listeners in list order, with MeasureSession first.
    • MeasureSession.kt grew from 1000 to 1039 lines. All of that is the mandated R3 pooling plus the §3.5 shared hit, with no new feature logic.
  • Room v3:
    • The migration matches 3.json (verified by script and by MigrationV3SchemaTest). Existing rows backfill to PROXY_BOX, and the other columns are NULL-tolerant.
    • Regeneration: new file, then one UPDATE, then delete the old file, under writeLock and NonCancellable, with a re-check under the lock.
    • Meshes: never regenerated; they fall back to a cache box, and the row is untouched.
    • K10: saveTemplate and saveMesh both commit through commitLocked → commit → check(bytes ≤ MAX_SCAN_BYTES).
  • AR lifecycle:
    • The anchor is detached in onSessionPaused while the session is still live, and also on pickUp, on a target change and on a failed drop.
    • close() only drops references.
    • A repeated frame timestamp changes nothing.
    • Pause drops the fallback plane and offers the fallback again.
    • Process death restores the target, the spin and the space reading.
    • The lights requirement is set by PlacementController only, and the host keeps SceneView's lights only then.
  • Recon:
    • Truncation: μ = max(4 cm, 3v).
    • Weights: round(2·conf/255·s/z²), clamped to 1..64, saturating at 127. There is no Int overflow (127·32767 + 64·32767).
    • Ray walk: a projective SDF in z-depth units, at v/2 Euclidean steps. Its NGP cells are monotone, so the "last" dedupe is enough.
    • C1: the behind band ends at 0.5μ.
    • C2: Sutherland–Hodgman clipping with welded cut vertices.
    • C3: the QEM point is clamped to the cell's vertex box, so the output never leaves the input's bounding box.
    • C4: the generated table gives consistent face segments and face-safe fans. All 256 cases and random fields are tested watertight.
    • C5: never smaller than the original form, since max(L, √2·r̄) ≥ √2·r̄.
    • Memory: at N_MAX, VolumeSpec guards dims product ≤ Int.MAX/3. VolumeSizing grows the voxel until the fence-posted count fits, and the 2.5 m cap keeps the voxel under 3 cm (worst case about 2.7 cm on low RAM).
  • K2:
    • Place uses ArScreenAdGuard, never enters a Measure visit and never calls recordCompletedScan.
    • Saved → Place calls onVisitLeftWithoutAd, which drops any pending chance.
    • The gallery item that resumes after Place finds nothing to consume. MeasureVisitTrackerTest covers both paths.
  • K1 and K5: Place imports only app.pro.ProFeature, never app/billing. onOpenPaywall is accepted and unused, because Place is Free.
  • Strings: all 66 place_* keys have Hindi, including gallery_kind_furniture, and the placeholders agree.

Missing tests

  • A mixed-axis verdict (MAJOR 1): one axis TOO_BIG, the other TIGHT with a wide band; and a FITS case where the smallest clearance is not on the min-score axis.
  • The real recon pipeline into writeMesh, saveMesh and modelForPlacement (MAJOR 2).
  • A floor AREA showing the "height not checked" note (MINOR 3). A fallback line on a raised surface (MINOR 4).
  • PlaceViewModel: a repository failure shows Failed, not Deleted (MINOR 5).
  • A MeasureSession pool test: no sample in two places at once, and a drop-oldest return, using a fake channel or an extracted SamplePool.
  • Recon: a sofa-near-a-wall scene (MINOR 8), an upper bound on the ± (MINOR 10), and integration producing a thin-part case for the saturation rule (MINOR 7).

Verdict

Mergeable for the device gate after MAJOR 1. MAJOR 2 must be resolved before the D (3D scan) milestone integrates saveMesh. No BLOCKERs. The MINORs can ship with tickets. None of the findings is a regression of pre-existing behaviour; all are in new code.

Not checked

  • Nothing was run: no Gradle, no tests and no device. The pass/fail claims above are the orchestrator's and the latest result XML's, not mine.
  • SceneView 4.65 behaviour (bytecode not inspected this time):
    • whether Node(apply = …) re-runs apply on recomposition. If it does, NodeHolder.set re-hides the model at the HUD's 10 Hz recomposition rate, and it would flicker for up to a frame.
    • createModelInstance(ByteBuffer) buffer lifetime.
    • whether KHR_materials_unlit is honoured, and the mipmaps for minFilter 9987.
  • On a device:
    • 30 fps on Place.
    • colour fidelity of the unlit photo face, and lighting on the Place host.
    • real ARCore hit normals on point hits.
    • thermal behaviour and peak PSS of recon.
  • Not read line by line: GlbWriterV2Test (only skimmed), SyntheticScenes.kt, and SymmetricEigen3 (assumed deterministic; it is pre-existing engine code).
  • Out of scope: Builder B's Pro, billing, ads, Settings and AppContainer changes, beyond K1, K2 and K5 and the template-source wiring line.
  • Not checked in detail: the CI workflow, the manifest and backup-rule diffs, and the SpaceView.html and HANDOFF.md content.
Reviewsdocs/reviews/P1-pro-review.md · updated 16 Nov 2026, 11:30

P1 Pro foundation: review (security + correctness)

  • Reviewer: FRIDAY, §4.B review with §4.D (MASVS), §4.K (CI) and §7.
  • Scope: Builder B's uncommitted diff against 4f8ec1f.
    • app/pro/*, app/billing/*, ads/AdsSdk.kt, ads/AdsManager.kt.
    • AppContainer.kt, MainActivity.kt, settings/SettingsScreen.kt.
    • The manifest and both backup XMLs, app/ and data/build.gradle.kts, libs.versions.toml, ci/*, android.yml.
    • strings_pro.xml (EN and HI) and the tests under app/src/test/.../{pro,billing,ads}.
    • Builder A's Place, M4 and recon code is out of scope.
  • Risk class: HIGH (payments, §4.D).
  • Method: I read the tests first, then the diff, then every call site.
    • I did not run Gradle (orchestrator's instruction).
    • Build and test evidence is the orchestrator's green run (app 217 tests, data 63) plus the result XMLs already on disk. Paths are cited below.

Summary

Severity Count
BLOCKER 0
MAJOR 3
MINOR 7

The verification core is sound:

  • The RSA check is correct and fails closed.
  • Pending purchases are never granted or acknowledged.
  • Refunds, revocations and account hold take Pro away at the next query.
  • Release builds cannot reach the fake gateway.
  • The cache is excluded from backup and transfer.
  • CI pins resolve to the right tags.

The three MAJORs are all on the edges of the state machine and the product surface:

  • Cold start: a common return path still initialises AdMob for a Pro user.
  • Clock rollback: winding the clock back inside the grace window extends the grace without limit.
  • Paywall honesty: the paywall sells a gallery limit that isn't enforced.

Top security risk: offline-grace abuse through the wall clock (MAJOR 2). It needs no tools and no APK patching, so it sits below the ADR-004 threat bar ("patched APK") that the design accepts. It is also a stated invariant (§4.4) that the code and its test claim to satisfy.

Verified correct (evidence)

Purchase verification

Signature check (PurchaseVerifier.kt:22-64):

  • Uses KeyFactory("RSA") with X509EncodedKeySpec, then Signature("SHA1withRSA").
  • Runs over the UTF-8 bytes of Purchase.originalJson (PlayBillingGateway.kt:157-158).
  • This is Play's scheme. Only java.security is used; there is no custom crypto.
  • A blank, garbage or non-base64 key or signature makes publicKey return null and verify return false.
  • Covered by PurchaseVerifierTest (14 tests: flipped byte, tampered data, wrong key, empty, non-base64, blank and garbage key).

Release fails closed:

  • PLAY_LICENSE_KEY is required when REQUIRE_RELEASE_CONFIG=true (app/build.gradle.kts:37-38).
  • When the key is missing or unparsable, purchasesEnabled=false (AppContainer.kt:106). The paywall then shows NOT_ON_SALE, purchase() returns NotConfigured without launching, and the verifier rejects everything. Nothing is granted and nothing is sold.
  • Debug builds take the fake gateway's own key (AppContainer.kt:92-93).

Can release use FakeBillingGateway? No.

  • Release hard-codes FAKE_BILLING = "false" (app/build.gradle.kts, release block). Only debug and release build types exist; there is no initWith.
  • The R8 output from the 2026-11-06 17:01 release build confirms it:
    • FakeBillingGateway, FakeBillingControlsKt, $NextOutcome and $Companion appear in app/build/outputs/mapping/release/usage.txt (removed).
    • They have no class mapping in mapping.txt. The only hits are $$compose source-info lines, which are mapping-only.
  • The Settings debug panel sits behind the same constant (SettingsScreen.kt debugPanel), and billing is always the Play gateway in release.

Pending is never granted.

  • fromPurchases grants only state == PURCHASED && !suspended (Entitlement.kt:137).
  • PENDING maps to Entitlement.Pending. It holds no cache and is never acknowledged.
  • UNSPECIFIED is ignored.
  • Tests: pending purchase gives Pending…, pending payment then bank approval unlocks Pro, and forged pending purchase does not show Pending.

Acknowledgement:

  • Only verified, PURCHASED, unacknowledged purchases are acknowledged (Entitlement.kt:153).
  • A failure is retried on every refresh (start, foreground every 10 minutes at most, paywall open, Restore).
  • The cache records success (EntitlementRepository.kt:259-271).
  • Tests: acknowledgement failure is retried after a process restart and forged purchase … never acknowledged.

Play-reported fields can't be forged on their own.

  • OwnedPurchase.state, productIds and suspended come from the Purchase object, which the library parses out of the signed originalJson.
  • So a fake billing service can't change them without breaking the signature. Only a patched APK can, and ADR-004 accepts that.

Products:

  • Grants are limited to ProCatalog.proProductIds = {"pro"}.
  • queryActive asks for SUBS only, and the prepaid pass30 is a SUBS base plan.
  • Suspended (held or paused) subscriptions are excluded by default and also filtered.
  • enablePendingPurchases(...enablePrepaidPlans()) is set (PlayBillingGateway.kt:58).

obfuscatedAccountId: not used. That is correct for an account-less app: a per-install id would break Restore on reinstall. See MINOR 4 for the consequence.

Entitlement state machine

  • Refund, revoke or expiry: QueryResult.Ok is authoritative. A missing purchase means Free and the cache is cleared (Entitlement.kt:155-159). Test: refund or revocation turns Pro into Free….
  • Grace boundary: at 7 d it is still Pro; at 7 d + 1 ms it is Free (Entitlement.kt:122). Tests cover 6 d 23 h 59 m, exactly 7 d, and 7 d + 1 ms, so an off-by-one would be caught.
  • Prepaid pass expiry: Play stops returning the purchase, so the next Ok query means Free. While offline, the pass can run up to 7 days past its expiry (accepted grace semantics).
  • Purchase updates never take Pro away, and a forged update never grants (Entitlement.kt:92-106, two tests).
  • Concurrency: one Mutex covers refresh, update and acknowledge. Grants are idempotent by token hash. Test: refresh racing a purchase grants once and acknowledges once.
  • Backup and transfer: datastore/spaceview_entitlement.preferences_pb is excluded in backup_rules.xml and in both the <cloud-backup> and <device-transfer> sections of data_extraction_rules.xml.
    • The path matches ENTITLEMENT_DATASTORE_NAME and DataStore's files/datastore/<name>.preferences_pb layout.
    • It is enforced by ProPersistenceTest.entitlementFileIsExcludedFromBackupAndTransfer.
    • Nit: the XML comments call this BackupRulesTest.
  • Tamper evidence: the cached record is plain DataStore holding a SHA-256 of the token, with no MAC. Editing it requires root, which is inside the accepted ADR-004 threat model, and it can grant at most 7 days. This is acceptable as recorded (Entitlement.kt:46-47, shortcut:).
  • Unknown at cold start:
    • AdsManager.adsAllowed starts false, and canShowAds needs adsAllowed, so there is no ad while Unknown.
    • A cached Pro inside the grace window is published as soon as the DataStore read finishes (EntitlementRepository.kt:126-128), so in the common case there is no Pro flash and no ad flash.
    • The exception is MAJOR 1.

Gating and ads

  • FeatureRules.evaluate (FeatureGate.kt:48-59): only Pro gets the Pro allowance, so Unknown, Free and Pending gate as Free. The count limits are 20, 3 and 2 (ProCatalog.kt:88-90). check() waits at most 1 s, then falls back to Free.
  • Lapse never hides data: gates only answer questions about new actions. No read, view, share or delete path consults them. FeatureGateTest has a 40-item case.
  • Ads for Pro: onEntitlement(Pro) drops the interstitial and the pending chance and sets canShowAds=false. BannerAd returns early, which disposes the AdView (BannerAd.kt:58-59), so banners disappear after a purchase.
    • startSdkIfAllowed and gatherConsent short-circuit on !adsAllowed before any UMP call.
    • The Settings privacy row is hidden for Pro.
  • MeasureVisitTracker (contract K2): MeasureVisitTracker.kt has no diff. The Free path is unchanged, and the 18-test suite gained cases (MeasureVisitTrackerTest, +44 lines).

Paywall (Play policy)

  • Close button: a 48 dp IconButton with a content description, first in focus order. System Back also closes.
  • Prices: every price comes from ProductDetails, and the strings contain none.
  • Yearly price: shown as "₹799 / year". It is not presented as a monthly cost.
  • Terms: the trial text states its length, what it converts to, the price and how to cancel. The prepaid text says it doesn't renew.
  • Links and Restore: the Manage deep link (…/subscriptions?sku=pro&package=…) and Restore appear on both the paywall and Settings.
  • Buy is disabled while a payment is Pending.
  • No AR, no hostage: the only openPaywall caller today is Settings, and Place passes the paywall callback but never calls it. Closing the paywall pops back to where the user was.
  • Hindi: 74/74 keys, and the placeholders are reordered correctly (for example pro_terms_trial uses %3$s %2$s).
  • TalkBack:
    • The plans form a selectableGroup of rows with Role.RadioButton.
    • The title is a heading.
    • The message uses a polite live region.

CI and supply chain

Action pins: every pin matches its tag. I checked with git ls-remote --tags today:

Action Pinned SHA Tag
actions/checkout 3d3c42e5… v7
actions/setup-java b843ebf9… v6
gradle/actions 8da46b53… v6^{} (the peeled commit, which is correct)
actions/upload-artifact cf430e03… v7

Secrets:

  • PLAY_LICENSE_KEY is only tested with [ -z ] and never echoed.
  • Fork PRs get no secrets on pull_request. Their release build then has a blank key, which fails closed, with a warning.
  • The workflow keeps permissions: contents: read.
  • The key is a public key and ships in the APK by design.

Dependencies: there are 12 new transitive release dependencies; ci/release-dependencies.txt is updated. Billing 9.1.0's POM pulls in transport-* and play-services-location:19.0.0. I unzipped the AARs from the Gradle cache:

AAR What it declares
play-services-location-19.0.0 No permissions
places-placereport-17.0.0 No permissions
transport-backend-cct / transport-runtime INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE (already allowed); services and receiver exported="false"
billing-9.1.0 com.android.vending.BILLING, <queries>, two ProxyBillingActivity entries with exported="false"

The merged release manifest (app/build/intermediates/merged_manifest/release/.../AndroidManifest.xml, 16:53) has no location permission, and its permission set equals ci/allowed-permissions.txt (8 entries).

androidTest compile: :data:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin was added to the unit and lint step.

Robolectric migration test

Scope of the Windows exclusion:

  • The filter is inside :data's tasks.withType<Test>() and keys on the Gradle JVM's os.name.
  • It excludes only com.spaceview.data.SpaceViewMigrationTest, so Linux CI runs it.
  • isFailOnNoMatchingTests=false only matters for --tests runs on Windows.

Does it exercise both migrations? Yes.

  • It calls runMigrationsAndValidate(DB, 2, true, MIGRATION_1_2) and (DB, 3, true, MIGRATION_2_3), plus a full chain from v1 to LATEST_VERSION.
  • Each call validates against the exported data/schemas/.../{1,2,3}.json, added to test assets in data/build.gradle.kts.
  • It then opens real Room and reads the rows back.
  • robolectric.properties pins sdk=35 (below compileSdk 37). This is reasonable.

Findings

BLOCKER

None.

MAJOR

1. A Pro user whose cache is older than 7 days gets UMP and MobileAds.initialize at cold start: EntitlementRepository.kt:118-128, AdsManager.kt:147-149

  • Problem:
    • start() publishes the cache only when it is Pro inside the grace window.
    • Otherwise the entitlement stays Unknown until Play answers.
    • Two independent 1 s timeouts both resolve a slow answer to Free:
      • the repository's compareAndSet(Unknown, effective(cached)), which gives Free for a stale cache;
      • AdsManager's withTimeoutOrNull(1000) ?: Free.
    • The Free path calls gatherConsent (UMP requestConsentInfoUpdate, and the consent form where required), then MobileAds.initialize once canRequestAds() is true. The SDK can't be de-initialised.
  • Scenario:
    • A yearly subscriber who measures a few times a month opens the app 8 days after the last open.
    • The cache is 8 days old, so effective gives Free.
    • The first Play connection plus queryPurchasesAsync takes over 1 s, which is routine on a cold low-end phone or a slow network (connect timeout 10 s).
    • At 1 s the user becomes Free, so UMP runs (in the EEA/UK a consent form can appear to a paying user) and MobileAds.initialize runs on the cold-start path.
    • Play answers Pro at about 1.5–3 s. If the Home banner loaded in between, it flashes.
    • The same happens on every reinstall or new phone, where there is no cache at all.
    • The approved decision is "AdMob never initialised for Pro". AdsManagerProTest Unknown - no ad for 1 s, then treated as Free codifies the current behaviour.
  • Fix (small): let ads wait for a settled entitlement instead of 1 s.
    • Add EntitlementRepository.settled: StateFlow<Boolean>, set true after the first APP_START refresh returns Ok or Failed.
    • AdsManager.start waits for settled with a generous cap (for example 12 s, above CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS), then follows the entitlement.
    • Ads have no cold-start urgency: Free users see their first banner a few hundred ms later.
    • Gates keep their 1 s wait, since Unknown already gates as Free.
    • Replace the codifying test with "Unknown for 5 s, then Pro: zero consent requests and zero inits", plus a stale-cache case.
  • If skipped: the headline Pro promise ("no ads, AdMob never initialised") breaks for the most common return pattern of an episodic utility app. That is also a privacy surface (consent form, ad-SDK network traffic) for paying users.

2. Rolling the clock back inside the grace window extends offline Pro without limit: Entitlement.kt:118-127

  • Problem:

    • effective() rejects a clock that is more than 5 minutes before confirmedAt.
    • It trusts any clock between confirmedAt and confirmedAt + 7 d.
    • Nothing records the latest time the app has seen, so moving back to a point inside the window isn't detected.
    • Both the KDoc ("winding the clock back can never extend the grace") and ARCHITECTURE §4.4 ("a rollback never extends grace") claim otherwise.
    • The test clock moved back past the confirmation never extends grace checks only rollbacks to before confirmedAt.

  • Scenario:

    1. Buy pass30 once (₹149) and let the app confirm it on day 0.
    2. Disable the Play Store app (Settings → Apps → Disable, allowed on most phones). startConnection then returns BILLING_UNAVAILABLE, which becomes QueryResult.Failed, which falls back to the cache.
    3. Turn off automatic time and set the date to day 1.
    4. Whenever the clock nears day 7, set it back to day 1.

    Pro (no ads, unlimited gallery) then lasts indefinitely, with no root, no patched APK and no tools. That is below the ADR-004 bar ("a patched APK skips the check").

  • Fix: persist a high-water mark and reject time travel below it.

    • Add lastSeenMillis to CachedEntitlement. On every evaluation (start, foreground, timeout path), write max(lastSeen, now).
    • effective() returns Free when now < lastSeen − CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_MS, and measures age as max(now, lastSeen) − confirmedAt.
    • The grace is then bounded by 7 days of app-observed time.
    • Optionally also add elapsed realtime within one boot.
    • Add reducer tests: "clock set back to inside the window after lastSeen → Free" and "small NTP correction under lastSeen → still Pro".
    • Correct the KDoc and the §4.4 row.

  • If skipped: the 7-day grace becomes an unlimited free Pro for anyone willing to disable the Play Store. The revenue at risk is small (ADR-004), but the code ships a false security claim in the HIGH-risk path.

3. The paywall sells "Unlimited gallery saves", but the 20-item Free cap is enforced nowhere: ProCatalog.kt:106, with no call site for featureGate

  • Problem:
    • GALLERY_UNLIMITED is shipped = true, so ProCatalog.advertised lists it as a Pro benefit (pro_benefit_gallery).
    • pro_reason_gallery tells users "The free gallery holds 20 items."
    • But AppContainer.featureGate has no consumer: grep finds no featureGate or check(GALLERY_UNLIMITED outside pro/.
    • The project's own rule (ProCatalog.kt:51-53, PLAN §9 "Pro honesty") is to flip shipped in the same change that ships the gate.
    • This is the brief's known gap. Its impact is the false advertising, not lost data.
  • Scenario: a Free user saves 35 items unhindered. The paywall (from Settings → Free plan) tells them Free stops at 20 and that Pro adds "Unlimited gallery saves", which they already have. A buyer who paid partly for that benefit got nothing extra. That is a misrepresentation risk under Play's subscription and deceptive-behaviour policies, and a support-ticket and refund risk.
  • Fix: either set shipped = false for GALLERY_UNLIMITED until the gate lands (the paywall then advertises only No ads), or enforce the gate in these three places:
    1. Scan entry, before any AR session (ADR-005 rule 1): in AppNavHost.kt:107 (Home onScan) and AppNavHost.kt:202 (Gallery onScan), before navigate(Routes.SCAN):
      • when (featureGate.check(GALLERY_UNLIMITED, galleryCount)) { NeedsPro -> openPaywall(GALLERY_UNLIMITED); else -> navigate(SCAN) }
      • This needs a cheap @Query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM gallery_items") suspend fun count() and an observeCount() for the "18 / 20" counter. No count query exists today, and observeAll().size would load every row.
    2. Save backstop: in ScanViewModel.save (ScanViewModel.kt:234-243), before store.save(draft), on the non-AR Review step. This covers a lapse or a second device between entry and Save.
      • On NeedsPro, keep the draft in the ViewModel and show "Gallery full" with Upgrade (paywall; on return with Pro, save), Share and Discard.
      • Never drop the measured result (§5.1 rule 2: never hold a result hostage).
      • The cleanest single point is a gating ScanStore decorator in :app (:data must not depend on :app/pro).
    3. Every other gallery insert: the same check goes before GalleryRepository.saveTemplate and saveMesh (K10, Builder A). saveMesh also checks DEVICE_SCAN against a mesh-item count (FREE_DEVICE_SCANS = 3) when that feature ships.
    • Existing items above 20 stay viewable, placeable, shareable and deletable. Only the next save is gated, as FeatureGateTest already specifies.
  • If skipped: the first paid release advertises a limit and a benefit that don't exist.

MINOR

4. A genuine signed purchase can be replayed indefinitely; prepaid expiry and packageName are not checked: Entitlement.kt:135-139

  • Problem:
    • The verifier proves only that Google signed the JSON. A genuine originalJson and signature (for example one ₹149 pass30, extracted on a rooted phone and shared) can be served forever by a fake billing service on any device, because nothing binds it to an account or a time.
    • ADR-004's table only discusses forged JSON.
  • Scenario: a leaked expired pass grants Pro on every device that runs a billing emulator.
  • Fix:
    • For non-auto-renewing purchases, parse purchaseTime from the signed JSON and refuse it when purchaseTime + 31 d < now. The same value also caps the offline grace at the pass's real end.
    • Optionally check packageName == BuildConfig.APPLICATION_ID (cheap belt-and-braces).
    • Record "replay of a genuine purchase" as an accepted residual risk for auto-renewing plans in ADR-004.
  • If skipped: this accepted risk class stays slightly wider than documented.

5. PLAY_LICENSE_KEY isn't validated at build time; a wrong but parsable key means users are charged, never granted, then refunded: app/build.gradle.kts:37-38, AppContainer.kt:106

  • Scenario: the CI secret holds another app's licence key, or a stale one. purchasesEnabled is true, every real purchase fails the signature check, the paywall says "The purchase didn't complete", Play refunds after 3 days, and 1-star reviews follow.
  • Fix:
    • When REQUIRE_RELEASE_CONFIG=true, parse the key in Gradle (base64 → X509EncodedKeySpec → RSA) and fail the build if it is invalid.
    • Add a release-gate checklist line: one licence-tester purchase on the internal track turns Pro on before promotion (already in §4.10 device tests; make it gating).

6. Cold start does RSA key parsing twice on the main thread in onCreate: MainActivity.kt:32, AppContainer.kt:97-106

  • Problem:
    • container.ads.startAfterFirstFrame(this) touches ads, which builds entitlements eagerly in onCreate, before the first frame.
    • That calls PurchaseVerifier.forKey(key) and publicKey(key): two KeyFactory("RSA") parses, and the first JCA provider load.
    • In debug it also generates a 1024-bit RSA key pair and reads SharedPreferences on main.
    • The KDoc and MainActivity both say no billing work happens before the first frame.
  • Scenario: a release build with a real key adds an estimated 5–30 ms (unmeasured) to the ≤ 800 ms cold-start budget.
  • Fix:
    • Parse the key once (val key = PurchaseVerifier.publicKey(...), and derive purchasesEnabled from it).
    • Make the verifier lazy, or move container.ads.startAfterFirstFrame into the posted first-frame callback.
    • Verify with am start -W ×3, as §4.9 requires.

7. The paywall Close button scrolls off screen: PaywallScreen.kt:106-113

  • Problem: CloseBar is the first child of the verticalScroll column.
  • Scenario: on a small phone, or at 200% font size, the user scrolls to the plans and the terms, and the only visible dismiss is gone. Play wants a clearly visible dismiss. System Back still works, but it isn't visible.
  • Fix: move CloseBar above the scrolling column, in the same Surface.

8. purchase() takes the first outcome on the shared flow, not the one for its own flow: EntitlementRepository.kt:173, :208

  • Scenario: a PENDING purchase from an earlier session is approved and arrives on updates while the user is in a new flow. (This is narrow, because Buy is disabled only while the current entitlement is Pending.) The new flow then reports the old outcome, and its own outcome is dropped, because there is no subscriber and no replay.
  • Fix: match on the offer's product and base plan or on a token not seen before, or document it as accepted. The entitlement itself stays correct either way.

9. Test gaps against the brief's failure modes: EntitlementReducerTest, AdsManagerProTest

  • Covered:
    • A forged signature: the real RSA path runs through EntitlementRepositoryTest (forged purchase from a fake billing service never grants).
    • Pending to granted.
    • The grace off-by-one.
  • Missing:
    • A rollback inside the grace window (MAJOR 2).
    • PurchaseState.UNSPECIFIED never grants.
    • Cold start with a stale cache and slow Play gives zero UMP and zero init calls (MAJOR 1). Today's test asserts the opposite.
    • An onPurchaseUpdate that holds a valid purchase for a non-Pro product.
  • Fix: add those four cases.

10. Billing 9.1 brings Firelog/datatransport, which sends library diagnostics to Google: ci/release-dependencies.txt (+transport-backend-cct)

  • Scenario: the Data safety form says no diagnostics are collected by SDKs, but the billing library transmits them.
  • Fix: review the Play Billing SDK's data disclosure at submission (already flagged in §4.8 PRIVACY) and record the result in docs/.

Nits (not findings)

  • Both backup XMLs refer to "BackupRulesTest". The test is ProPersistenceTest.entitlementFileIsExcludedFromBackupAndTransfer.
  • pro_cta_trial renders "Start 7 days free trial". It should read "Start 7-day free trial", which needs a separate string or a plural-free phrasing. The Hindi is fine.
  • PaywallViewModel.buy doesn't guard Pending itself; the guard is in the UI only. Mirror it in the ViewModel.
  • FakeBillingGateway signs purchaseState as an enum name, while Play uses ints. That's harmless today because nothing parses the JSON, but MINOR 4's fix will parse it, so align the fake then.

Pre-existing (not regressions)

  • None found in the scoped files.

Verdict

Approve the foundation for merge, but not for release.

  • The verification, pending, acknowledgement, refund and backup paths are correct and well tested.
  • Fix MAJOR 1–3 before any build reaches the Play internal track with real products. MAJOR 3 can be closed in one line by setting shipped = false until the gate lands.
  • MINOR 5 should become part of the release gate.

Not checked

  • Builds and tests: I did not run Gradle. Pass and fail evidence is the orchestrator's green run plus the result XMLs dated 2026-11-06 in app/build/test-results/testDebugUnitTest/. I did not re-run them against the final tree.
  • The Robolectric migration test has never run: it is excluded on this Windows host, and CI hasn't run this diff. "Runs on Linux CI" is unverified until the first CI run shows TEST-com.spaceview.data.SpaceViewMigrationTest.xml.
  • R8 removal of the fake gateway: taken from the 17:01 release build's usage.txt and mapping.txt. I did not inspect the dex, and I didn't re-check after any later edit.
  • Device behaviour: real Play Billing (licence testers, slow or declined test cards, pending to approved, account hold, a second Google account), UMP in the EEA, the TalkBack pass, the Hindi rendering, and the cold-start time with and without the key.
  • ProGuard/R8 keep rules for billing reflection (the library ships consumer rules), and the size delta (+184 KiB was reported by Builder B, not measured by me).
  • Builder A's Place, M4 and recon code, and the SpaceView.html and ARCHITECTURE-v2.md edits, beyond the sections I cited.
  • CVE or OSV status of the 12 new transitive dependencies.

PLAN v3 gate: the review fix round on 2D v1 (Final Reviewer + Judge)

FRIDAY, 2026-11-24. Gate commit: 6afb9e3 ("PLAN v3 review fixes"), against 26dd340 (the reviewed tree). The working tree is clean.

It covers:

  • the orchestrator's MAJOR 1 fix (the ad guard on Distance);
  • Builder A's round: MAJORs 2–4 and the range/height MINORs 1–7, plus TESTING §23;
  • Builder B's round: MAJOR 5 and MINORs 8–11, plus TESTING §22.

I checked it against:

  • docs/reviews/PLAN-v3-review.md (0 BLOCKER, 5 MAJOR, 11 MINOR);
  • docs/PLAN-v3-2D.md (W2, W4, W5, W6, §5);
  • the last ~45 lines of HANDOFF.md (the builders' claims);
  • TESTING §22 and §23.

No source was edited and no Gradle task was run. This file is the only write.

Verdict: PASS WITH CONDITIONS

All 5 MAJORs are FIXED and verified in the code. MAJORs 2–5 each have a JVM test that fails on the old code. MAJOR 1 is Compose wiring: I verified it by reading the code, and a device item covers it.

All 11 MINORs are closed. MINOR 2 (the slope σ) and MINOR 9 (the ML Kit disclosure) are closed by tuning or documentation, and each keeps a device or submission check.

The fix round adds no BLOCKER and no MAJOR. It does add:

  • five MINORs (G1–G5);
  • one performance warning (W1);
  • two DOC items.

The two that matter most:

  • G1: the interval-based 500 m cap hides the walk guidance for targets of about 250–500 m.
    • The app keeps asking for a 7 m walk.
    • A sight 2 taken after a moderate walk is then reported as "Out of range: may be over 500 m". That happens even for a 300–350 m target that a 30 m walk would measure.
    • No number is wrong; the cap is honest. But the message points the user the wrong way.
  • G2: any hit beyond 8 m now produces "Something is in the way before the ground". That includes a hit on the open ground itself, so TESTING §23 item 7 ("At 12 m it usually says Too far for one sight") will not match on the device.

The Pixel 10a APK may go to the user. No MAJOR is open. I recommend that R1 (G1 + G2, a few lines each) lands first, so the device pass of §23 items 7–10 tests the behaviour that will ship. If it does not, amend TESTING §23 items 7 and 8 before the pass.

The user still has to sign off the honest limits (G4). The effective limits are:

  • 2-sight: a number up to about 350–400 m, and only with a ~30 m walk;
  • Ground: about 8.5–8.7 m at hand height, barely beyond Near's 8 m.

Home still says "Distance to any point you aim at, up to 500 m", and PLAN §5 still expects "30 m (Ground) inside ±".

How this was verified

  • Reading:

    • the full git diff 26dd340 6afb9e3, tests first;
    • all of RangefinderCore.kt;
    • RangefinderSession.onFrame;
    • RayTriangulation.solve and requiredBaseline;
    • RangeUncertainty.inverseLaw;
    • HeightAim.sideFace and groundBase;
    • in MeasureSession: onFrame, processCommitRequest, the resume and new-session paths, the worker loop and farBase;
    • HandsFreeDropper.onFrame;
    • FrameReaders.centreHit;
    • SurfaceChooser.choose;
    • CutoutPixels;
    • CutoutMaker;
    • ScanViewModel.onFrontPhoto, onPictures and chosenPicture;
    • in GalleryRepository: save, encodeCutout, encodeTransparentCutout, cutoutFromPhoto, updateDimensions and shareCopy;
    • AdsManager.maybeShowAfterSave;
    • the Rangefinder screen's Readout, phaseHint and Controls;
    • the EN and HI strings_range.xml;
    • TESTING §22 and §23, and the PLAN W2 diff.

  • Hand calculations with the default RangeErrorModel:

    • aim σ 2/480 rad;
    • heading σ 0.1° + 0.005°/s;
    • sigmaMargin 1.05;
    • a camera 1.45 m above the floor;
    • a floor σ of 2 cm;
    • a VIO scale σ of 1%.

  • Test results on disk (a script over the result XMLs):

    Module Tests Failures Errors Skipped Results written
    engine 236 0 0 0 11-24 15:57
    ar 160 0 0 0 11-24 15:57
    data 70 0 0 1 11-24 13:14

    These agree with the orchestrator's run. No source file under any module's src is newer than its results.

  • Not mine: Kover, assembleDebug/assembleRelease, lint (0 errors) and the release-dex debug-string check come from the orchestrator. CI on 6afb9e3 is not recorded in HANDOFF (see R5).

1. MAJORs from the review

# Finding Status Evidence Test

Ground blocked when the hit is above the floor by more than max(10 cm, 2% of range), when it is nearer than Ground's low95 (:235-239), or when the averaged Near point is above the floor (:240-245). RangefinderCoreTest.aHitAboveTheFloorBeyondNearRangeBlocksGround (the review's 9 m wall-foot case; the block survives the hit dropping out), aNearPointAboveTheFloorIsShownAsNearNeverAsGround (the 0.3 m box top at 3 m), aHitOnTheFloorItselfAgreesWithGround (no false block from a floor-plane hit). M4 The box-top fallback chose the wrong corner's vertical plane FIXED HeightAim.sideFace (HeightAim.kt:75-112) intersects the ray with the four vertical side faces, including the implicit c0 + c2 − c1 (:78). It takes the nearest crossing with t > 0 inside the face width ± FACE_MARGIN_M = 3 cm (:95, :163). It refuses beyond 75° of grazing, and its σ carries the corners' σ across the face leaking through the ray slope (:105). cornerUnderRay is deleted, and boxTop no longer takes forward. Exact for a box, as the review asked. Aiming slightly past a top edge reads the front plane a little high: (overshoot) × tan(depression), about 2 cm for 5 cm at 19°. That is inherent in any vertical-plane top and acceptable. HeightAimTest.aimingAtTheTopFrontEdgeOffCentreLandsOnTheFrontFaceNotABackCorner (the review's 10 cm case: 0.80 m, not 0.45 m), aDiagonalViewOfTheImplicitFourthCornerUsesItsSideFace, aTallWardrobeTopIsReadOnItsFrontFaceWhenTheTopCannotBeSeen, aRayMissingEveryFaceGivesNoPointAndAGrazingFaceIsTooSteep.

The bbox is only a trust check, raised to 0.85 per axis (:50-53, :62), and it counts any visible alpha (minAlpha = 1, i.e. confidence > 0.35), so faint legs keep a chair "whole". Colour under the alpha is kept (CutoutPixels.applyMask). PLAN W2 is corrected. CutoutMakerTest.trustedMaskKeepsTheWholeCanvasWithATransparentBackground (same w × h as the photo), faintThinPartsKeepTheScaleAndStayInThePicture (the review's chair-legs scenario), aMaskThatLeavesMuchOfTheOutlineEmptyKeepsTheRectangle. The first two fail on 26dd340 (it cropped to 28 × 28).

2. MINORs from the review

# Item Status Evidence / test

It still calls processCommitRequest(session, lastTracking), so a pending "+" keeps its timing: the commit uses the worker's fresh candidate, framePointsOk from the last real frame, and anchors from session/Plane, never from the stale Frame. Hands-free is unaffected: HandsFreeDropper is its own ArFrameListener, time-based, and only calls requestCommit(), which the next onFrame serves whether or not that frame is a repeat. latestCentreHit is kept on a repeat, so PlacementController still sees this camera frame's hit. Freeze and front capture wait for the next real frame, which is correct (a new image is needed). Resume: sessionStartMs is reset and sessionEpoch bumped on every resume (:390-393), so the worker resets its gate, stabilisers and surface model (:1021-1029).
