3. New issues from the fix round

# Severity Where Problem and concrete failure scenario Fix
G1 MINOR RayTriangulation.kt:140-142; RangefinderCore.kt:438-445 (walk), :405 The interval cap hides the walk guidance. The walk the app asks for is raised only by an Ok preview (:445). With the cap, the preview stays null until high95 ≤ 500, so for a far target the request stays at the value set at sight 1. Live is null beyond Near/Ground, so that value comes from DEFAULT_GUESS_M = 50 m: "Walk about 7 m". Below a = 0.5 the solve says TOO_UNCERTAIN ("walk further"). Between a = 0.5 and the cap, it now says OutOfRange, where before the fix it showed a preview and asked for 30 m. Scenario (a true 350 m target, default model): a ≈ 4.7 / walk. The user walks the requested 7 m and gets "Not accurate enough yet. Walk further sideways and retake sight 2". The screen still says "Walk about 7 m", so they walk to about 12 m and retake. The result is "Out of range: may be over 500 m" for a 350 m target that a 30 m walk measures. For 300 m the same thing happens for sights taken after about 8–10 m. No number is wrong, but the effective range is lower than "350–380 m with a 30 m walk", because the app never asks for that walk until the user has made about 16 m (350 m) or about 22 m (380 m) of it unprompted. (a) In solve, when distance ≤ maxRangeM but high95 > maxRangeM and the walk is under MAX_BASELINE_M, return Rejected(TOO_UNCERTAIN) ("walk further"). Keep OutOfRange for a point estimate beyond 500 m or a walk already ≥ 30 m. (b) In walk(), raise requiredBaselineM from the triangulated point's distance whenever solve gives a consistent point (Triangulation.point, outcome ≠ INCONSISTENT/BEHIND/NEAR_PARALLEL), not only from an Ok preview. Tests: at 350 m a 12 m walk gives TOO_UNCERTAIN; the guidance reaches 30 m before 16 m have been walked. → R1
G2 MINOR RangefinderCore.kt:260; TESTING §23 item 7 OFF_GROUND for clear ground. liveIssue reports OFF_GROUND whenever rawHit.distance > NEAR_MAX_M, even when the hit is on the ground and Ground is simply too uncertain. Scenario: with depth ON by default, aim at open paving 12 m away. ARCore returns a depth or feature point on the paving at about 12 m, which is not above the floor and not blocking. Ground is TOO_UNCERTAIN beyond about 8.7 m, so the screen says "Something is in the way before the ground…". TESTING §23 item 7 expects "Too far for one sight". Both messages say "use 2 sights", so the action is right, but the stated reason is false, and the device tester will log a failure. Report OFF_GROUND only when groundBlocked, and let a far floor hit fall through to GROUND_TOO_FAR or OUT_OF_RANGE. Test: a floor hit at 12 m gives GROUND_TOO_FAR; the 9 m wall-foot case still gives OFF_GROUND. → R1
G3 MINOR (device-gated) RangefinderCore.kt:221, :235-246, :472 How long the Ground block lasts depends only on the aim window restarting. It clears only when the window restarts, i.e. on a turn of more than 1° from the window mean or a non-TRACKING frame. (a) Slow drift never clears it: with the 15-frame window full, the newest ray leads the mean by about 7 frames × the rate, so a pan slower than about 4°/s never restarts the window. Scenario: aim at a kerb or a car wheel (blocked), then lower the crosshair slowly (about 2°/s) onto the open paving in front. The screen keeps "Something is in the way" on a real ground point until the user jerks the phone. (b) One noisy frame blocks the whole aim. At 7 m a single depth or feature point more than about 0.6 m short (below low95), or more than 14 cm high, blocks Ground for as long as the aim is held. That matters only when Near does not lock on the same noisy hits, i.e. roughly 6–8.7 m. (c) A block can carry over to the next aim: a block set during a LIMITED frame (the aim window is empty, so the generation is not bumped) carries into the next steady aim. Store the mean direction at which the block was set, and clear it when the current mean is more than AIM_MOVE_DEG from it, independently of the window restarts. Require 2 of the last 3 frames to agree before blocking on a raw hit beyond Near (keep one frame for an above-floor Near estimate). Bump the generation on clear() even when the window is empty. Tests: block, then drift 0.07°/frame for 2° onto the floor, and Ground returns; a single outlier hit among 30 floor frames does not block. → R2
G4 MINOR (copy + product decision) strings_range.xml:6 (EN), values-hi/strings_range.xml:5; PLAN-v3-2D.md:10, :19, :58, :112 The copy overstates the effective limits. Home says "Distance to any point you aim at, up to 500 m, always with ±". The effective limits are: about 8.5–8.7 m for one sight on the ground (Near ≤ 8 m), and a 2-sight number only up to about 350–400 m, with a ~30 m walk (and in practice less, until G1 is fixed). Beyond that the answer is "may be over 500 m". The plan is stale too: PLAN §5's "30 m (Ground) inside ±" cannot pass (TESTING now says 12 m is "too far"), and U2 and W4 still say "up to 500 m". The review's deviation note asked for the user's sign-off; it is still outstanding. User decision (B-list): accept the limits, or fund the zoomed-aim / longer-walk work. Then: the Home detail (EN/HI), e.g. "Distance to a point: close up, on the ground nearby, or far away with 2 sights (several hundred metres), always with ±". Then: amend PLAN §1/U2/W4/§5 to the as-built limits, and add them to the store "known limitations". → R4
G5 MINOR (low) Cutouts.kt:50-53 A single stray pixel defeats the 85% trust rule. The rule is a bounding box of any alpha ≥ 1 (confidence > 0.35). One stray pixel near each opposite edge makes the bbox span the outline, so the "a mask that lost a large part of the object keeps the rectangle" protection is defeated. Examples: a 0.4-confidence speck on the floor at the bottom, or on the wall at the top. Scenario: a chair whose legs come out at 0.1 (invisible), plus one floor speck at the bottom edge. The rule says REMOVED, and Review shows a legless chair at the correct scale. The damage is bounded: there is no distortion any more, the user sees it on the checkerboard, and "Undo cutout" is there. But this is exactly the case the rule exists for. Pre-fix the bbox needed alpha ≥ 128 (confidence ≥ 0.5), so specks had to be stronger. Use a robust extent: per axis, the span from the 1st to the 99th percentile of visible-alpha mass, or ignore rows and columns with fewer than about 0.5% of the opposite dimension visible. Test: legless mask + one speck → NOT_SURE; the faint-legs test still passes. → R3

Warnings (accepted, device-checked)

  • W1 (performance): Saving a transparent cutout now starts its PNG ladder at 1024 px (previously 512). Each rung re-runs downscale + bleedEdges + a full PNG deflate (GalleryRepository.kt:750-753):

    • bleedEdges builds a boxed List<Int> of every transparent pixel and runs up to 8 passes;
    • photo-like subjects end at 640–768 px, i.e. 3–4 rungs on a ~0.7 MP picture;
    • the same ladder runs on every dimension edit (under the gallery write lock) and on a cleanUp repair.

    Saving is off the main thread (withContext(cpu)), so there is no ANR risk, but the Save time is unmeasured. Device check (R3): time Save of a chair cutout, with a target of ≤ 2 s on the Pixel 10a. Cheap fix if it is slow: estimate bytes per pixel from the first rung and jump straight to the fitting side.

  • W2 (MAJOR 2 residual, by design): Ground can only be refused when ARCore returns some hit on the obstacle. A featureless car side, depth off, or a target beyond depth range still gives Ground for the floor behind it, labelled "Assumes the point is on level ground". The test aHitAboveTheFloorBeyondNearRangeBlocksGround itself shows Ground before the first hit arrives. Device item: TESTING §23 item 7 (9 m wall foot; record how often a number appears before the message).

  • W3: a millisecond window remains between the AR check and ad.show in maybeShowAfterSave (see M1 residual). It is common to all AR screens and pre-existing.

DOC

  • D1: CutoutPixels.kt:30 still documents step 2 as "crop to the subject's bounding box, which then maps to the measured W × H". That is the behaviour MAJOR 5 removed. → R5

  • D2: dead code left by the fixes:

    • RangeUi.canRetake (RangeUi.kt:49) is used only by RangeUiTest:29-31;
    • CutoutPixels.crop is used only by CutoutTest:115.

    Remove both with their tests, so nobody re-wires the old rule. → R5

Checked and found clean:

  • Real floor points are not blocked by a plane hit. centreHit prefers a tracked plane hit inside its polygon (FrameReaders.kt:78-82). On the floor it lies within about 0.1 m of Ground's distance, well inside low95 (about 0.6 m short at 7 m). aHitOnTheFloorItselfAgreesWithGround pins this.
  • In Measure, the W5 far base cannot reach the floor behind an obstacle. SurfaceChooser.choose returns any hit at any range, and the far base is used only after 5 frames with no hit (MeasureSession.kt:1059-1064). So the MAJOR 2 failure mode does not exist in Measure.
  • canRetake after an Ok or OutOfRange result is true, which is correct: a retake after walking further is the right next step.
  • Strings: EN/HI parity holds for every new key: range_issue_off_ground, the three measure_* keys and the changed range_assumes_level/range_out_of_range*. The deleted measure_aim_base/measure_aim_top have no remaining reference (they were replaced in instructionRes).

4. Conditions

# Owner What When Check
R1 Builder A G1: TOO_UNCERTAIN instead of OutOfRange while the walk is under 30 m and the point estimate is ≤ 500 m, and walk guidance from the triangulated point. G2: OFF_GROUND only when blocked. Three JVM tests (§3). Before the Pixel 10a pass of TESTING §23 items 7–10. Otherwise, amend §23 item 7 (a 12 m ground hit says "Something is in the way") and item 8 (the 7 m request until the preview fits) to the current behaviour. Tests green; the HANDOFF line.

Carried from the review (not new):

Reviewsdocs/reviews/PLAN-v3-review.md · updated 24 Nov 2026, 13:08

PLAN v3 (2D v1) review: commit 26dd340 against 756b2bd (W1–W7, Builders A and B, orchestrator wiring)

Reviewer: read-only, as in the previous reviews. This file is the only write. Scope: git diff 756b2bd 26dd340 (153 files, +5 505 / −13 221), checked against docs/PLAN-v3-2D.md. Context came from the last ~60 lines of HANDOFF.md (what the builders say they built, and the deviations they declared) and from docs/reviews/SM1-M5-review.md (format). Method:

  • Read in full:
    • engine/range/* and their tests;
    • RangefinderCore, RangefinderSession, app/range/*;
    • VerticalPlaneAim, HeightAim and HeightAimTest;
    • the MeasureSession diff;
    • CutoutPixels, PngEncoder, GlbWriter.writeCutout, the GalleryRepository diff, Cutouts.kt and SubjectSegmenter.kt;
    • the ScanViewModel, PlaceViewModel, gallery UI, pro/billing/settings, AppNavHost and HomeScreen diffs;
    • AdsManager (the guard, consent and show paths), CI android.yml, and TESTING §22/§23.
  • Commands: git plus one read-only Python script, which checked:
    • EN/HI key parity;
    • placeholder parity;
    • R.string references with no definition.
  • No Gradle task was run (as instructed), so no build, test or lint result here is mine.

Verdict: APPROVED WITH WARNINGS. No BLOCKER. Fix the 5 MAJORs before the Pixel 10a APK goes to the user; MAJOR 1 breaks a hard product rule.

Counts: BLOCKER 0, MAJOR 5, MINOR 11. The nits at the end are not counted.

BLOCKER

None. I found no crash path in the new code that normal use reaches; MINOR 7 is a defensive gap.

MAJOR

1. The Distance screen has no ArScreenAdGuard, so the UMP consent form (and, in a race, an interstitial) can appear over the AR camera: app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/nav/AppNavHost.kt:152-155; app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/ads/AdsManager.kt:200-203, :333-350, :387.

  • Problem:
    • The route comment says "no ads and no visit tracker". The visit tracker is correctly left out.
    • But ArScreenAdGuard is not an ad: it is the mechanism that keeps ads away from AR. Every other AR destination calls it (Measure :212, Calibrate :235, Scan, Place). Distance does not.
    • Without it, visits.arInForeground stays false while Distance is on screen. Three things then go wrong:
      • gatherConsent passes canShowForm = { !visits.arInForeground }, so the SM1-M5 gate G1/R2 fix ("re-check AR at form-show time") is bypassed.
      • maybeShowAfterSave decides with AdScreen.NON_CAMERA instead of CAMERA_AR (:387), so AdPolicy's BLOCKED_CAMERA_SCREEN never fires.
      • preloadIfUseful and preloadInterstitial are no longer suppressed.
  • Scenario A (consent):
    1. A first-run EEA user, or a user whose earlier consent request was deferred, lands on Home. onNonArScreenResumed → gatherConsent → the UMP request goes out over the network.
    2. The user taps "How far?" at once.
    3. The consent form arrives about 1–2 s later. canShowForm() is true, and the form opens as a dialog over the running AR session.
  • Scenario B (interstitial):
    1. Save a measurement and close Measure. Home resumes, waits up to 1.5 s for AR to leave, then maybeShowAfterSave starts its own scope.launch. Cancelling pendingShowJob on Home's pause does not cancel that inner job.
    2. Tap "How far?" inside that window.
    3. The decision returns SHOW with screen = NON_CAMERA, the activity is still resumed, and the ad covers the camera.
  • Fix:
    • Add ArScreenAdGuard(ads) at the top of the Routes.DISTANCE composable (or inside RangefinderArScreen, as Place does).
    • Optionally re-check visits.arInForeground immediately before ad.show(...) in maybeShowAfterSave.
    • TESTING §23 item 12 should add "first launch: tap How far? straight after Home; no consent form over the camera".

2. Distance "Ground" is shown for points that are not on the ground. Evidence that the ray hits something first is thrown away, and a Near/Ground conflict is settled by the smaller ±, so the shown ± can miss the truth by a wide margin: ar/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/ar/RangefinderCore.kt:201, :214-221; app/src/main/res/values/strings_range.xml (range_assumes_level).

  • Problem:
    • hit is dropped when it is beyond NEAR_MAX_M (8 m), even though a hit at 9 m proves the ray is blocked before the floor.
    • Ground is then computed for the floor behind the object.
    • When both readings exist, minByOrNull { bound95 } picks one without checking that they agree, or that the Near hit is actually on the floor (hit.y − floorY).
    • The badge says "Assumes level ground", but nothing tells the user that the aimed point must be on the ground.
  • Scenario (camera 1.45 m, defaults, aim σ ≈ 0.004 rad):
    1. The user aims at the foot of a wall or a parked car, 0.2 m above the paving, 9 m away. ARCore returns a depth hit at 9.0 m, which is discarded (> 8 m).
    2. The ray's depression is atan(1.25/9) = 7.9°, so Ground gives 1.45 / sin 7.9° = 10.5 m.
    3. Its rel95 is about 8.6 %, inside the 10 % gate, so the screen shows about "10.5 m ± 0.9 m · Ground". The truth (9.0 m) is outside the ±.
    4. A near case: a box top 0.3 m high, 3 m away, with no Near hit that frame. Ground says 3.8 m ± 0.15 m.
  • Fix:
    • Keep the raw hit regardless of range.
    • Refuse Ground when any hit along the ray is nearer than the Ground distance minus its ±95.
    • Refuse Ground when the Near point is above floorY by more than a few σ.
    • Rename the badge to "Assumes the point is on level ground".
    • Add a RangefinderCoreTest with an off-floor hit at 9 m.

3. Tracking loss during the RESULT phase is not recorded, so "Retake sight 2" can triangulate across a tracking loss: RangefinderCore.kt:191-198, :272-277; RangeUi.kt:48; RangefinderScreen.kt:367.

  • Problem:
    • Loss detection and path accumulation run only while phase != RESULT.
    • retakeSight2() checks lostSinceSight1, but nothing sets that flag during RESULT.
    • The spec's rejection rule (W4: "Rejected if tracking was lost between sights") is therefore not enforced on the retake path.
  • Scenario:
    1. Sight 2 is refused ("different things"), and the retake button is offered.
    2. The user lowers the phone. The camera is covered, or points at a blank sky, so ARCore goes PAUSED. It then recovers, and the world frame may have shifted.
    3. The user taps Retake, walks and takes sight 2. walk() sees lostSinceSight1 == false, and solve(..., trackingLostBetween = false) returns a number from two frames that may not match.
    4. pathLength also missed the walk made during RESULT, so σB is understated.
  • Fix:
    • Run the bookkeeping whenever sight1 != null, including RESULT. Alternatively, record a loss in every phase.
    • Add a test: result → NOT_TRACKING frames → retakeSight2() returns false, or the next result is TRACKING_LOST.

4. The scan box-top fallback chooses the wrong corner's vertical plane in ordinary poses, giving a large, systematic height error that the ± does not cover: ar/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/ar/HeightAim.kt:150-155, :178-194; ar/src/test/kotlin/com/spaceview/ar/HeightAimTest.kt:92-107.

  • Problem:
    • cornerUnderRay picks the corner whose vertical line has the smallest lateral offset from the ray. It does not prefer the nearest corner, and it sets no maximum offset.
    • It also ignores the implicit 4th corner, c0 + c2 − c1. That corner is diagonal to c1, so in a diagonal view the nearest corner is often missing and c1, the far corner, sits exactly on the ray line.
    • The fallback runs whenever the hit is not on the top face. This is the common case when aiming at a top edge: the hit lands on the front face just below it.
    • The test passes only on a tie: all three offsets are 0.5 m, and index 0 wins.
  • Scenario (the test's own box: front edge z = −2, back edge z = −3, 0.8 m tall, camera 1.5 m):
    1. The user aims at the top front edge 10 cm right of centre. The ray passes 0.40 m from the front-right corner and 0.35 m from the back-right corner.
    2. The back corner is chosen, so the plane is 1 m too far.
    3. The ray is pitched down about 19°, so the top lands at 1.5 − 3·tan 19.3° ≈ 0.45 m instead of 0.8 m.
    4. For a wardrobe taller than the eye (TESTING §23 item 5), the same mistake overstates the height.
  • Fix:
    • Intersect the ray with the four vertical side faces of the measured prism (all 4 corners) and take the first face hit in front of the camera, within the face's span plus a margin. That point is exact for a box.
    • Failing that, consider all 4 corners and choose the nearest along the ray among those within a lateral tolerance (for example, max(5 cm, 2 % of range)); refuse otherwise.
    • Add tests for the off-centre and diagonal cases.

5. A cutout is cropped to the mask's bounding box and then stretched to the measured W × H, so a loose or partial mask distorts the object by up to 2× and the Review shows a different shape from Place: app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/scan/imaging/Cutouts.kt:41-54; ScanViewModel.kt:253-258; data/.../GalleryRepository.kt (encodeCutout, the GLB quad at w.meters × h.meters); GalleryImages.kt (aspectRatio(b.width / b.height)).

  • Problem:
    • The rectified front photo is already metrically W × H: its edges are the measured outline. Cropping it further to the subject's bbox and mapping that crop onto W × H stretches it.
    • MIN_BOUNDS_SHARE = 0.5 allows a 2× stretch on each axis.
    • Thin parts below confidence 0.5 (chair legs, table legs, cables) fall out of the bbox. The seat is then stretched down to the floor line.
    • The Review and the gallery draw the cutout at the bbox aspect, but the GLB in Place uses W × H, so "what the Review shows is what is stored" does not hold for the geometry.
    • The Review then says "only the object is saved, at its measured size", which is not true of the picture.
  • Scenario:
    1. Scan a chair (Other). The legs come out at 0.3–0.45 confidence, so the bbox covers the top 65 % of the outline.
    2. Review shows a squat, legless chair on the checkerboard.
    3. Place shows the seat and back stretched 1.54× vertically, standing on the floor, at "true size".
  • Fix: don't crop. Keep the full rectified canvas, with alpha from the mask, so the quad stays exactly W × H and the picture stays undistorted. Keep the bbox only for the trust check, and raise it to about 0.85 on each axis. If the plan's "bbox maps to W × H" wording is kept, it is the plan that needs correcting: the rectified photo already is the mapping.

MINOR

  1. The 500 m cap and TESTING §23 promise more than a noisy estimate can deliver: RayTriangulation.kt:125; TESTING §23 items 9 and 10; RayTriangulationTest.kt:45, :75.

    • The cap is applied to the point estimate.
      • A true 600 m target with a 30 m walk has a parallax σ of about 13 %, so about 7 % of results show a number (e.g. "480 m ± 180 m"). That is honest, but it breaks "never a number".
      • A true 480 m target reads "out of range" in about 40 % of runs.
    • "Walk 1 m on a 200 m target → near-parallel" can instead give "Not accurate enough yet", because the measured angle is noisy (σ ≈ 0.33°).
    • The Monte-Carlo test lifts the cap (Double.MAX_VALUE), so how often a real target near 500 m is reported as "out of range" is never measured.
    • Fix: either word TESTING as "usually" and accept, or use a cap rule on the interval. For example: out of range when the low end is > 500; a "> 500 m?" hint when the interval straddles 500.

  2. The Ground level-ground σ (0.15°, a 1 : 380 slope) is optimistic outdoors: RangeErrorModel.kt:230.

    • Paving with a 1 % cross-fall (0.57°) at 12 m is off by about 8 %, against a shown ±95 of about 9.5 %. A 2 % fall is outside the ±.
    • The badge covers this in words, but the ± is the product's promise.
    • Fix: take this to the device test (TESTING §23 item 7) and be ready to raise the value to about 0.4°.

  3. The W5 far height base is Ground only (declared deviation; acceptable), but Measure never tells the user it assumes a level floor, and the source can flicker: MeasureSession.kt:1034-1058.

    • A committed HitKind.GROUND base has no "assumes level floor" note in the result. Distance has the equivalent badge.
    • When the base aim alternates between a real hit and GROUND, each frame resets the other stabiliser (:1058), so the lock may never complete.
    • Fix: show a note for GROUND endpoints, and stop the stabilisers from resetting each other on a single-frame switch.

  4. The vertical-plane top assumes the aimed top is directly above the base, and the ± has no term for an offset: VerticalPlaneAim.kt:68-90.

    • If the base is 10 cm in front of the door line, the height is off by 10 cm × tan(pitch): 17 cm at 60°.
    • Fix: the Measure hint and the Help should say "base exactly below the top". Consider adding a small offset term to the ±.

  5. The Retake button does nothing after a pause during RESULT: RangefinderScreen.kt:367; RangefinderCore.kt:306.

    • reset() sets lostSinceSight1 = true, so retakeSight2() returns false.
    • For an Ok result (rejected == null), the UI still offers Retake.
    • Fix: expose canRetake from the core in RangeState.

  6. W6 tuning is mostly diagnosis: MeasureSession.kt:453-512.

    • The plan's "tune" items were not done: TrackingGate, SampleStabilizer and SurfaceChooser are unchanged, and the "depth points usable immediately" path is not visible. The diagnosis may justify that, but TESTING §23 items 1–2 must decide it.
    • The main thread still does the hit test and the depth-patch copy for every repeated SceneView frame; only the worker skips them. Skipping those frames at the main thread, as RangefinderSession.onFrame:103 does, saves CPU.
    • sessionStartMs is not reset on pause/resume within one session, so after a resume the diagnostics times are not measured from the resume.
    • The repeated-frame skip itself is correct:
      • lastTs is the last processed timestamp, so DROP_OLDEST cannot starve sampling;
      • TrackingGate ignores dt ≤ 1e-4;
      • DwellTrigger is time-based (ns), so hands-free timing is unaffected.

  7. Sight(...) validates with require on the AR main thread: RangefinderCore.kt:341, :383; RayTriangulation.kt:21.

    • A non-finite ray or σ from a bad frame would throw from onFrame and crash.
    • It is unlikely with the current inputs, but the rule is "never crash".
    • Fix: check isFinite first, or wrap the construction in runCatching and skip the frame.

  8. Cutout texture budget: GalleryRepository.CUTOUT_TEXTURE_SIDES.

    • An RGBA PNG of a photo at 512 px is roughly 400–600 KB, so with MAX_SCAN_BYTES = 500 000 most cutouts end at 320–384 px (declared "may look soft").
    • If even 256 px doesn't fit, encodeCutout silently saves a plain panel after the Review showed a cutout.
    • Fix: record the size actually chosen in TESTING §22 item 17. Consider alphaMode MASK with a JPEG + separate alpha, or a per-item budget exception for cutouts.

  9. ML Kit Subject Segmentation is a beta library (16.0.0-beta1), and it bumps ML Kit common/vision-common: gradle/libs.versions.toml, ci/release-dependencies.txt.

    • The Data safety notes defer the key check: "check that subject segmentation is covered by the same disclosure".
    • Before release:
      • re-run TESTING §21 (the naming chip);
      • confirm on Google's live ML Kit disclosure page that subject segmentation is covered, and record the date read.
    • The EN/HI privacy text is accurate: on-device, diagnostics through Play services, no "everything stays on your phone".

  10. The CI debug-absent grep does not cover the W6 debug HUD: .github/workflows/android.yml:157.

    • The HUD is behind BuildConfig.DEBUG, a constant, so R8 strips it. A cheap regression guard is to add dbg track to the grep list.
    • W7 itself is sound:
      • FAKE_BILLING is a constant false in release (app/build.gradle.kts:145), and release is minified;
      • the switch and the button sit only inside if (BuildConfig.FAKE_BILLING);
      • their texts are unlocalised literals, so the dex grep is meaningful.

  11. TESTING §23 item 5 ("aim above its front corner") and §22 item 12 ("at the measured W:H") describe behaviour the code does not have yet (MAJOR 4 and MAJOR 5). Update them with the fixes.

Deviations declared in HANDOFF: judgement

  • Ground works only to about 13 m, and 2-sight at 500 m ends near ±160 m: acceptable as honest engineering. It is a product decision, though:
    • PLAN §5 acceptance "30 m (Ground) inside ±" cannot pass by Ground;
    • a 500 m reading is "Rough" (±32 %).
    • The user must sign off on it, or on the proposed zoomed-aim and longer-walk work, before a store listing says "up to 500 m".
  • W5 far base Ground only (no 2-sight): acceptable for v1. See MINOR 3.
  • Depth ON by default (orchestrator): correct and consistently wired: MeasureSettingsRepository.kt:93, :218, plus MeasureUiSettings, ScanSettings, RangeUiSettings and the Help copy. Delete my data returns it to the new default.
  • Cutout texture ≤ 512 px and the help key name: acceptable (MINOR 8, nit).

What I verified OK

  • Range maths:
    • Ground: d = h / sin θ, with (σd/d)² = (σh/h)² + cot²θ·σθ².
    • Closest approach of two rays: the s/t formulas are correct.
    • The expected miss is projected on the common normal, one axis per error source.
    • The 7-source central-difference Jacobian is measured from sight 2.
    • The inverse-law bound d·a/(1−a) is the correct upper half-width for d ∝ 1/angle, using σ evaluated at the measured parallax; it is conservative on the low side.
    • The refusal order is correct: tracking lost → parallel → behind → angle < 0.5° → miss > 3.5σ → unbounded.
  • Monte-Carlo tests: not tautological. The truth is independent of the estimator, and the inputs are drawn from the model (aim on both sights, heading drift on sight 2, baseline σ, VIO scale). They test linearisation and coverage. They cannot test whether the model matches reality; that is the device test's job.
  • RangeFormat: reuses Units' ± rounded up and value-to-leading-place rule ("500 m ± 18 m", decimal feet). It never shows more digits than the ±.
  • RangefinderSession:
    • it is a proper ADR-001 primary listener (configures the session, depth only when wanted and supported);
    • it skips repeated frames and runs on the main thread only;
    • pause and new-session reset the core, and a pending 2-sight becomes TRACKING_LOST;
    • events go through tryEmit into a buffered flow;
    • close() never touches the session.
  • VerticalPlaneAim:
    • the sign and geometry are correct;
    • the 75° grazing refusal works;
    • the σ is the aim × 1/cos g plus the base-depth leak;
    • with the plane re-oriented every frame, the point does not jump while the aimed top is above the base: that line lies in every such plane;
    • HEIGHT composes the vertical difference.
  • W1 removal:
    • no dangling code reference;
    • R.string references all resolve, and EN/HI key and placeholder parity is complete (only the non-translatable app_name is EN-only);
    • furniture, scan3d and the pro strings were removed in both locales;
    • Room stays v3;
    • legacy TEMPLATE and MESH rows place from their stored GLB, or from a cache box (no crash); a template is not editable (the UI hides Edit and the repository refuses it);
    • GLB_VERSION is unchanged, so legacy GLBs stay "usable";
    • ProCatalog / GallerySaveGate API trimmed cleanly; PaywallDestination maps a removed feature name to NO_ADS (tested);
    • "Delete my data" no longer keeps a 3D quota key.
  • W2/W3:
    • pixels are straight alpha end to end, and the PNG encoder is correct (filters, CRC, IHDR RGBA8);
    • edges are bled before the PNG, so there is no dark halo from black transparent pixels;
    • the alpha-weighted downscale is correct;
    • the GLB quad winding and UVs are correct (unlit, double-sided, BLEND only with PNG);
    • the segmenter is null-safe: a 10 s timeout, cancellation propagates, the client closes when the task completes, LinkageError and missing Play services fall back;
    • share sends image/webp with a .webp name;
    • Place: CENTER origin with 2 mm thickness, so the bottom edge rests on the floor and the quad sits 1 mm off the wall; the fit check uses the row's W/H/D, never a zero depth.
  • Orchestrator: Routes.DISTANCE and the Home row are wired; there is no visit tracker (correct). The guard is missing: see MAJOR 1.

Nits (not counted)

  • Home now has both "Distance" (measure) and "How far?" (rangefinder). Make sure the detail lines tell them apart in Hindi too.
  • The live RangeIssue.OUT_OF_RANGE from Ground is unreachable for a camera below about 2.2 m, because the 0.25° depression check comes first. It is harmless.
  • help_templates_title / help_templates_body are now about cutouts; rename the keys when convenient.
  • place_mesh_fallback says "3D shape unavailable" for any fallback box; for a legacy template "model unavailable" would read better.

Summary

  • Counts: BLOCKER 0 · MAJOR 5 · MINOR 11. Verdict: approved with warnings; fix the MAJORs before the device APK.
  • Top risks:
    1. Ads/consent over AR: Distance lacks ArScreenAdGuard (MAJOR 1). This is a one-line fix and a hard product rule.
    2. Wrong numbers with a confident ±:
      • Ground accepts off-ground points (MAJOR 2);
      • the scan box top uses the wrong corner plane (MAJOR 4);
      • a retake after a tracking loss is triangulated anyway (MAJOR 3).
    3. Cutouts distorted by up to 2× because the mask's bbox is stretched to W × H (MAJOR 5). Don't crop; keep the full rectified canvas with alpha.
  • Verified OK:
    • the W4 maths and error propagation, including the inverse-law bound and non-tautological Monte-Carlo tests;
    • the honest display rounding;
    • the RangefinderSession lifecycle and threading;
    • the vertical-plane geometry, the grazing refusal and the leak term;
    • the repeated-frame skip (no starvation, dwell unaffected);
    • depth ON wired everywhere;
    • W1 removal with no dangling references, full EN/HI parity, legacy rows placing without a crash, Room v3;
    • W7 test unlock unreachable in release;
    • straight-alpha and PNG correctness;
    • flat-Place geometry;
    • an accurate privacy text (pending the live ML Kit disclosure check, MINOR 9).
  • Deviations:
    • The declared range limits (Ground ~13 m, ±160 m at 500 m) are honest but need the user's sign-off against PLAN §5.
    • The Ground-only far base is acceptable for v1.

SM1 + M5-remainder gate: Smart Measure SM1, UMP/review/Help/About/Delete, accessibility, N2 (Final Reviewer + Judge)

FRIDAY, 2026-11-17. Gate tree: the uncommitted work on top of 13f3740. It covers:

  • SM1 Smart Measure (Builder A): the hands-free dwell drop, ML Kit naming, G2, accessibility in A's screens, and recording CaptureMethod.HANDS_FREE;
  • the M5 remainder (Builder B): UMP consent, in-app review, Help/FAQ, About/OSS, Delete my data, the accessibility pass, N2, and the store-build guards;
  • both fix rounds for docs/reviews/SM1-M5-review.md (3 MAJOR, 13 MINOR).

I checked it against HANDOFF.md (the Phase 3 entries), docs/reviews/SM1-M5-review.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE-v2.md §5 (with the as-built notes and the tick-off decision), §4 and §12.3 K6, docs/PLAN.md §9, docs/TESTING.md §17, §20 and §21, and docs/research/android-performance.md §6.3. No source was edited and no Gradle task was run; this file is the only write.

Verdict: PASS WITH CONDITIONS

All 3 MAJORs are FIXED and verified in the code or docs. All 13 MINORs are closed (MINOR 15 by a heuristic whose residual risk is tracked by a device item). The fix rounds introduce no new BLOCKER or MAJOR.

I found two new MINORs from the fix rounds and one doc set:

  • G1: the consent form can still open over an AR screen. The AR check runs when the request starts, not when the form is shown, so a user who opens Measure during the network round-trip gets the form over the camera. Hands-free is safe, because window focus suspends it. But TESTING §20 item 5 promises "never over Measure", and §21 item 8 tells testers to expect it there.
  • G2: the new "+" tap guard is not reset by Undo or Clear. A deliberate "+" within 1 s of an auto-drop, after an Undo and a small (< 3 cm) correction, is swallowed silently. That is exactly the precision correction the guard should never block.
  • G3–G5: doc drift (DOC).

There are three conditions, all small: R1 and R2 are code (a few lines each, with a test), and R3 is docs, commit and CI.

RC readiness: the app is feature-complete for the Phase 3 RC, apart from the user's configuration and D step 2. On-device 3D scan is correctly not advertised: ProCatalog.kt:124 has DEVICE_SCAN shipped = false, and the paywall lists only shipped benefits (:136). What remains is release work, not features (§5):

  • device passes;
  • M6 polish (EmojiCompat, the skybox, lint plurals);
  • store artefacts (listing, privacy-policy text, known limitations);
  • the user's secrets and Play Console set-up.

1. MAJORs from the review

# Finding Status Evidence
M1 Hands-free dropped points behind the calibration picker, and they reached known-length calibration FIXED Gate: the dropper runs only when HandsFreeGate.active(enabled, suspended, windowFocused) (HandsFree.kt:90-92, :128-130). SideEffect writes it, and LocalWindowInfo.isWindowFocused is snapshot state, so focus changes recompose. Measure: passes suspended = handsFreeSuspended(calibration, sessionFailed, frozen), which is true for CalibrationStep.Choosing (MeasureScreen.kt:139-144, :221-222), and startOff = calibration != null, so calibration starts with hands-free off. Clear on choice: onChooseReference goes through startCalibration(ref, session::clear), which clears before Measuring (:196, :228-231). This also closes the review's step 6 (one stray point plus the user's first tap). Scan (ScanArScreen.kt:131) and Furniture (FurnitureMeasureScreen.kt:137) suspend on non-outline steps, freeze, failure and complete. Every enable edge holds off 1 s (HandsFreeDropper.kt:99-105). Tests: HandsFreeGatingTest.neverWhileThePickerCoversTheReticle and aDialogOrTheSwitchStopsIt pin the rule, and choosingAReferenceClearsThePoints pins the clear. They fail against the old behaviour (no suspension, no clear; strictly, the old tree lacks the functions). HandsFreeDropperTest.dropsWhenEnabledAndNeverWhileSuspended covers the dropper side. Residual: the Compose wiring itself (the SideEffect and focus read) is code-read only; TESTING §21 item 4 covers it on a device.
M2 ML Kit diagnostics were missing from the Data safety plan, and the privacy text overclaimed FIXED Data safety plan: android-performance.md §6.3 (:303-306) adds an ML Kit row (diagnostics, device/app info, device or other IDs; collected, not shared; images labelled on-device) and a Play Billing datatransport row, and keeps "photos, measurements, 3D models: not collected". TESTING §17 (:173-181) has the same ML Kit answer with the disclosure page's date, the in-app review row, the "one consistent story" rule, and the list of dependencies whose change triggers a re-check. In-app copy: help_privacy_title is now "your measurements and photos stay on your phone" (strings_help.xml:37). The body names AdMob, Play purchases and ML Kit diagnostics, and lists exactly what Delete removes and keeps (:38), which matches UserDataEraser.kt:20-37. about_privacy_summary_detail is changed the same way (:55). The HI text matches (values-hi/strings_help.xml:36-37, :53). Backup claim checked: "stored only on this phone" holds, because the backup rules include only datastore/ and exclude calibration and the entitlement (backup_rules.xml, data_extraction_rules.xml). Test: none applies; this is a copy and doc fix, verified by reading. Not verified by me: the live Google disclosure pages.
M3 SM1 shipped on by default with an unverified haptic tick and no device checklist FIXED Tick off: HAPTIC_TICK_ENABLED = false (HandsFree.kt:148), and its only use is guarded (:107). ARCH §5.1 as-built records the decision and its reason. Checklist: TESTING §21 exists with 20 items: dwell tuning (1–3), no unintended drops (4–8), the tick experiment on a debug build only (9), TalkBack (10–12), the ML Kit chip with and without the model, offline, and on every bump (13–16), the merged manifest and cold start (17–18), and the G2 floor (19–20). Every check the review asked for is present. Test: none applies (a constant and a doc).

# Item Status

12 ML Kit failures silent; inner cancel rethrown FIXED: an ML Kit-side cancel becomes an IOException (MlKitObjectNamer.kt:55). LabelObjectNamer rethrows only the caller's cancellation (ensureActive), and reports every failure to onFailure, which logs one WARN per process with no PII (:27-32). The version is pinned with a comment (libs.versions.toml). Tests: theCallersCancellationIsNotSwallowed, failuresAreReportedAndAnInnerCancellationIsJustNoSuggestion. sdkinternal fallback: it catches LinkageError → MlKit.initialize (:89-95). This is acceptable, but note that MlKitContext ships in the APK (the R8 mapping keeps it as c), so a removed API breaks the build, not the runtime. The fallback is belt and braces; the real guard is §21 item 16 on each bump.
13 The store-build guard accepted malformed values FIXED: the same email and https rules apply in Gradle (app/build.gradle.kts:51-62) and in AppLinks (AppLinks.kt:40-45), with a "change both together" note.
14 Help didn't mention hands-free FIXED: a "Hands-free points" section (what it does, both switches, Undo) and the accuracy line (strings_help.xml:11, :14-17). HI is equal.
15 G2: a reflection under a tracked glossy floor could win FIXED (heuristic): a strong point-only bin must also cover ≥ AREA_RATIO² × the plane bin's x–z scatter determinant (FloorEstimator.kt:174-183, :244). Test: aReflectedTableBelowATrackedFloorPlaneNeverWins fails under the pre-fix "strong" rule. Both aStronglySupportedPointFloorBelowATablePlaneWins (G2) and aLongWatchedMirroredLineOrSpotNeverBeatsAPlaneFloor (T-D0 MINOR 3) still hold. Builder A was right to reject the reviewer's "within 0.3 m below the plane" idea. G2's own case is a coffee table about 0.45 m above an untracked floor, so a 0.3 m band would block the very floor G2 must find. Height can't separate the two cases, but the area of the aimed-over evidence can. Residual risk: the scatter is of reticle hits (PlacementCore.kt:149), not of surface extents, so it compares where the user aimed. A user who aims over a small patch of tracked floor and then dwells over a large reflected bed outside the plane's polygon could still flip the floor. This is device-gated (§21 item 20, with AREA_RATIO tunable). It is no worse than the T-D0 status quo, and I accept it as a warning (W2).
16 No test of the session-side dwell contract FIXED: the AutoDropSource seam plus HandsFreeDropperTest (5 tests: suspended, count-decrease hold-off and no re-drop, freeze edge, the allowed table, the ignoreTap table). autoDropTarget uses AutoDropRules.allowed (MeasureSession.kt:514-523).
Nit 1 N2 waits "≤ 5 s" in HANDOFF Not re-checked (HANDOFF text only).
Nit 2 The ARCH §5.1 "unchanged" line FIXED: §5.1 as-built now lists the session's small read-outs.
Nit 3 Import order Left to lint (no finding).

CaptureMethod.HANDS_FREE is recorded through session.anyHandsFreePoint() (Measure: MeasureViewModel.kt:129; Scan: ScanDraftBuilder.kt:174). The test is CaptureMethodTest, and there is no schema change (v3 column).

2. New issues from the fix rounds

# Severity Where Problem and scenario Fix
G1 MINOR (residual of MINOR 10) AdsManager.kt:196-207; AdsSdk.kt:69-81; TESTING :340, :382 Problem: the AR check happens before requestConsentInfoUpdate. loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired then runs in that request's success callback, whatever screen is in front by then. Scenario: offline first launch, later back online. The user resumes Home, which starts the retry, and taps Measure within the network round-trip (about 0.5–2 s). Or, on a first EEA launch, the user taps onboarding's "Calibrate now" at once. In both cases the UMP form opens over the camera. Hands-free does not drop behind it (the window loses focus, M1), and no policy forbids the form there. But TESTING §20 item 5 says "never over Measure, Scan or Place", while §21 item 8 tells testers to put "the consent form on a fresh EEA install" over the camera. The two contradict each other, and one of them will be reported as a failure. Give AdsSdk.requestConsent a canShowForm: () -> Boolean (= !visits.arInForeground). In the success callback, when it is false, skip the form, call back with a new ConsentResult.DEFERRED, and reset consentRequested so the next non-AR resume shows it. Add one AdsConsentTest case (AR becomes foreground between the request and the form → no form; the next non-AR resume shows it). Change §21 item 8's example to "the camera-permission dialog or the notification shade". → R2
G2 MINOR (regression in the MINOR 5 fix) MeasureSession.kt:240-242, :481-491, :544-566 Problem: lastAutoAtMs/lastAutoPosition (and completedAtMs) are set on commit but never cleared by undo() or clear(). Scenario: the dwell drops point 1 two centimetres off a corner. The user taps Undo (about 0.4 s) and nudges about 2 cm to the true corner. The deliberate "+" lands about 0.9 s after the drop, within 3 cm of the undone point, so ignoreTap returns true and nothing happens, with no message. The dwell won't place it either, because re-arming needs a 3 cm move from the last drop spot (aRemovedPointHoldsOffAndTheSameSpotIsNotDroppedAgain). The user has to tap again after the 1 s window. Precision corrections of a few cm are exactly the case the guard must never block. It can't lose data, so the severity is MINOR. In undo() and clear(), set lastAutoAtMs = null; lastAutoPosition = null; completedAtMs = null: the user acted, so the tap is no longer a "confirmation". Add a test: either extract a tiny TapGuardState (record auto, record complete, onPointsRemoved, ignore(now, target)) next to AutoDropRules and table-test it, or extend HandsFreeDropperTest. → R1
G3 DOC AndroidManifest.xml:22-25 The VIBRATE comment still says "the one short tick after a hands-free point drop uses performHapticFeedback". The tick is now off. Say "off (HAPTIC_TICK_ENABLED); if ever enabled it uses performHapticFeedback, which needs no permission". → R3
G4 DOC ARCH :1446 (§12.3 K6) The contract row still reads suggest(jpeg). As built, it is suggest(jpeg, kind: ObjectKind? = null) (ObjectNamer.kt:36; §5.2 as-built records it). Update the K6 row. → R3
G5 DOC TESTING :364 (§20 item 20) "Known open items for Builder A … see HANDOFF". HANDOFF says they are done (48 dp mode tabs MeasureHud.kt:437, the Scan AR rows, the spoken Review rows ScanReviewScreen.kt:236-253). Replace it with a check: "Measure, Scan and Furniture HUDs: tabs ≥ 48 dp, Review rows read in full". → R3

Checked and found clean:

  • Can a legitimate "+" be swallowed apart from G2?
    • The completion guard only ignores a second "+" within 1 s of completing, which would otherwise clear() the result just made. That is the intended behaviour.
    • A tap with no current candidate within 1 s of an auto-drop is ignored. The old path would have requested a commit that, with the phone still there, ends in SAME_SPOT. This is acceptable.
    • With the hands-free switch off, lastAutoAtMs is never set, so the guard never fires.
  • Can hands-free stop working for good after a dialog? No.
    • isWindowFocused is snapshot state read in composition (HandsFree.kt:90), so regaining focus recomposes, and SideEffect sets enabled = true again, with the normal 1 s hold-off.
    • Nothing latches. The other inputs (suspended, the switch) are recomputed every composition.
    • Split-screen or freeform loses focus only while the user is in the other window; touching SpaceView restores it.
    • The worst case is the HUD switch reading "on" while focus is elsewhere. That is cosmetic.
  • The consent retry path:
    • It is idempotent (consentRequested CAS, reset only on a failed or gone result).
    • It is a no-op for Pro (adsAllowed false) and before start() (entitlementJob null).
    • No ad request precedes consent (startSdkIfAllowed checks canRequestAds()).
    • Offline, it re-asks once per non-AR resume, which is cheap.
    • Only G1 remains.
  • Lint and Hindi:
    • The app has 6 warnings, all pre-existing types; ar and data are clean.
    • EN/HI parity is 708 = 708 with placeholders matching.
    • The new a11y_*_one and fraction keys exist in both locales.
    • The HI fractions use "सही"/"बटा", which reads naturally.

  5. Hindi sign-off by a native speaker (PLAN §9), including the TalkBack readings of fractions and "कम या ज़्यादा".
  6. Decisions:
    • D step 2: run the spike, or confirm "no 3D scan in v1.0";
    • W1 (keep hands-free on by default after the §21 tuning);
    • W3 (card/A4 calibration);
    • the phone models for the device set.
  7. Then: internal track → closed test with 12 testers for 14 days (personal account) → production with a staged rollout.

Release gate (FRIDAY §6.2) as of this gate

Line Status
All BLOCKER and MAJOR closed and verified in code ✅ for SM1-M5 (3/3); R1 and R2 are MINORs
CI green on the release commit (unit, lint, coverage, size, alignment) ⏳ local EXIT 0; CI on the RC commit owed (R3)
Migrations tested, including an on-device upgrade ⏳ JVM migration tests in CI; on-device over TD0/M4 is a user item (B4)
Critical journeys on a low-end and a mid-range device ⏳ user (B4)
Security pass; Data safety and privacy policy match behaviour ⏳ code side ✅ (no new exported component; permissions = allowlist; no upload path; UMP before ads); the form and policy are A3/A4 + B1/B3
Performance budgets on a release build (start-up, frame time, ANR paths, size) ⏳ size ✅ (estimate); cold start and 30 fps owed on a device (§14, §21 item 18)

Known limitations and release notes written ❌ A3
Rollback plan: staged rollout, previous AAB kept ❌ A6

6. Recommendations for Phase 3

  1. Order:

    • R1 and R2, which are tiny;
    • R3 (commit and green CI);
    • the M6 polish in one builder pass (EmojiCompat, skybox, plurals), with a size and cold-start re-check;
    • the drafts (A3, A4);
    • the user's secrets, then the tag build;
    • the internal track.

    Don't let the store drafts wait for device work; they are independent.

  2. First device pass priority (one evening on the user's phone):

    • §6 bench (accuracy is the product);
    • §21 items 1–8 (hands-free on by default touches every flow);
    • §20 items 1–6 (consent);
    • §21 items 13–14 (ML Kit chip).

    If §21 items 1–2 show eager or missing drops, tune HOLD_NS within 0.6–0.8 s before anything else. If it stays bad, flip the default off (W1) rather than ship a fight with the user.

  3. Haptic tick: leave it off for v1.0 regardless. Item 9 is an experiment for v1.1, not an RC blocker.

  4. Data safety: fill the form from the A4 sheet on the day of submission, after re-reading the four Google disclosure pages (AdMob, ML Kit, Play Billing, Play Core). Re-check it whenever ci/release-dependencies.txt changes in the listed groups (TESTING §17 :181). com.google.android.odml:image:1.0.0-beta1 arrived transitively with ML Kit; note it in the dependency audit, though it is not a finding.

  5. D step 2 stays behind the spike. If it slips past the RC, v1.0 ships without on-device 3D. The paywall already says nothing about it, so nothing in Pro needs to change.

  6. After the closed test: watch Play vitals for the ANR-prone paths this milestone added (the first ML Kit init on Default, the DataStore read at Home resume for the review). Both are off main by design; vitals will confirm it.
