Reviewsdocs/reviews/SM1-M5-review.md · updated 17 Nov 2026, 16:05

SM1 + M5-remainder review: Smart Measure SM1 (Builder A) and the M5 remainder + N2 (Builder B)

Reviewer: FRIDAY §1, §4.B (standard and thermonuclear passes), §4.D (ML Kit, UMP, data deletion), §4.E (dwell and announcement per-frame cost, cold start), §4.J (accessibility). Read-only: this file is the only write. Scope: all uncommitted work on top of 13f3740 (git status, git diff HEAD, and every untracked file listed there). Method:

  • Read order: the tests (DwellTriggerTest, SpokenTextTest, ObjectNamerTest, UserDataEraserTest, ReviewPrompterTest, FeatureGateTest), then the diff, then the call sites. These included MeasureSession (commit path, freeze, pause, setMode), MeasureScreen/MeasureHud (calibration steps), ArSessionHost/ArRequirements, AdsManager.start/gatherConsent, EntitlementRepository.start, GallerySaveGate/GatedGalleryStore, GalleryRepository.cleanUp, ResultCards, Units.kt (imperial formatting), and the TESTING, ARCH and research docs.
  • Evidence is file:line that I read in this session.
  • I ran no Gradle task (as instructed: RAM is low and the orchestrator builds). So no test, lint or merged-manifest result here is mine.
  • Commands run:
    • git;
    • one read-only Python script for EN/HI key parity, placeholder parity and file parity across every strings*.xml, and for unused string keys.

Verdict: APPROVED WITH WARNINGS. No BLOCKER. The 3 MAJORs must be fixed before release (MAJOR 1 before the RC goes to testers).

Counts: BLOCKER 0, MAJOR 3, MINOR 13. Three nits are listed at the end and not counted.

  • Where the findings are:
    • All 16 are regressions in the new code or docs. None is a pre-existing defect.
    • MINOR 10 sits next to a pre-existing guard (app/build.gradle.kts:51-63 is unchanged from HEAD); the new part is the stricter runtime check in AppLinks.
  • What is clean:
    • The dwell core (DwellTrigger, SteadinessFilter extraction, the MeasureSession read-outs) is sound, single-threaded and allocation-free per frame.
    • UserDataEraser is complete for user content and is correctly scoped away from Pro and consent.
    • N2's wait is bounded.
    • The review prompt's policy edges hold.
    • Strings are at full EN/HI parity.
    • There is no Room schema change (SpaceViewDatabase.kt:32 is still version = 3; GalleryDao.deleteAll is a query only; captureMethod was already a v3 column, and CaptureMethod.HANDS_FREE already existed at ScanDraft.kt:12).

BLOCKER

None.

MAJOR

1. Hands-free keeps dropping points while the reticle is hidden behind the calibration picker, and the stray points carry into known-length calibration: app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/measure/MeasureScreen.kt:83, :100-102; MeasureHud.kt:114, :128; ar/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/ar/HandsFreeDropper.kt:63-82; MeasureSession.kt:285-286.

  • Problem:
    • The dropper's enabled follows only the setting and the HUD switch (HandsFree.kt:79-80).
    • During CalibrationStep.Choosing the HUD hides the reticle and the controls (MeasureHud.kt:114) and shows ReferencePicker (:128), but the AR session runs and the dropper keeps firing.
    • The Calibrate route starts in MeasureMode.DISTANCE (AppNavHost.kt:229), and "Known length" also measures in DISTANCE (MeasureScreen.kt:93-96). setMode returns early when the mode is unchanged (MeasureSession.kt:286), so nothing clears the hidden points when the user picks Known length.
    • In known-length mode the live length is deliberately hidden (gate R2, MeasureScreen.kt:98, MeasureHud.kt:119-121), so the user can't see that the span is wrong.
  • Scenario:
    1. Settings → Recalibrate (hands-free is on by default).
    2. The picker appears over the camera. The user holds the phone still over a table while reading the three options for about 2 s: a 1 s hold-off from session start, about 0.5 s to lock, and the 0.7 s hold.
    3. Point 1 drops, unseen. A natural 3 cm hand drift re-arms the dwell, and point 2 can drop too.
    4. The user taps "Known length". The mode doesn't change, so both points stay. isComplete is already true, so KnownLengthCard appears at once (MeasureHud.kt:129-135) for a span the user never chose.
    5. The user types their tape length. A factor inside 0.9–1.1 (Calibration.kt:154, :249) is accepted and scales every measurement in that ARCore session.
    6. With only one stray point, the user's own first tap completes a span that starts at the stray point.
  • Fix:
    • Gate the dropper on what is on screen: dropper.enabled = handsFree.enabled && calibration !is CalibrationStep.Choosing. One way is a suspended input on rememberHandsFree that each screen sets when its reticle or Controls are hidden.
    • Also call session.clear() in onChooseReference before calibration = Measuring(ref). That way calibration always starts from zero points, even with hands-free off.
    • Consider defaulting hands-free off inside calibration, where the aim must be exact (card corners are 5.4 cm apart; the dwell's drift tolerance is 1 cm). The user can still switch it on from the HUD.
    • Add a JVM test on the screen's gating rule (no drop while Choosing).
  • If skipped: accuracy is the #1 priority, and a silent wrong calibration is the worst kind of error. In practice the ±10 % gate rejects most stray spans, which leaves the user with an unexplained "check failed" on the first calibration attempt, and a rare accepted one corrupts the session's scale.

2. ML Kit's (and the other SDKs') diagnostics are missing from the Data safety plan, and the in-app privacy text says "everything stays on your phone": app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (ica meta-data), app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/smart/MlKitObjectNamer.kt:27-33; docs/TESTING.md:168-173; docs/research/android-performance.md §6.3; app/src/main/res/values/strings_help.xml:32-33, :50.

  • Problem:
    • Inference is on-device, and the photo is never uploaded (correct, MlKitObjectNamer.kt).
    • However, the Play-services ML Kit client sends API-usage diagnostics to Google. ARCH §5.2 (ARCHITECTURE-v2.md:525) says so. Google's ML Kit data-disclosure page lists device and app information, performance metrics, API configuration, error codes and an installation identifier. The release dependency list now also carries firebase-components and the com.google.mlkit common modules (ci/release-dependencies.txt).
    • The planned Data safety answers don't mention this:
      • TESTING §17 lists only Billing (+ datatransport), AdMob and UMP.
      • android-performance §6.3 lists AdMob only, and says that photos and measurements are "not collected".
    • The new Help and About copy headlines "Privacy: everything stays on your phone" (strings_help.xml:32, :50). It also says "Delete my data removes everything SpaceView has saved" (:33), but the eraser deliberately keeps the ad counters, the review record and the entitlement cache (UserDataEraser.kt:33-38).
  • Scenario:
    • The user submits the RC with the Data safety form filled from TESTING §17. ML Kit's "App info and performance → Diagnostics" (and, per the current disclosure text, "Device or other IDs") are undeclared.
    • Play's User Data policy requires the form, the privacy policy and in-app disclosures to be accurate and consistent. An undeclared SDK collection is a rejection or enforcement risk, and "everything stays on your phone" contradicts the form once that collection is declared.
  • Fix:
    • Add an "ML Kit (image labelling via Play services)" row to TESTING §17 and to android-performance §6.3: diagnostics collected by Google, not shared, not user content. Mark it "verify against Google's ML Kit data-disclosure page at submission", as ARCH §5.2 already requires.
    • Re-check the form whenever com.google.mlkit changes in ci/release-dependencies.txt.
    • Reword the Help title to something true, e.g. "Privacy: your measurements and photos stay on your phone". Keep the body, and add one clause: "Google's services used by the app (ads, purchases, object naming) send them diagnostic data".
    • Change "removes everything SpaceView has saved" to "removes your measurements, Gallery, calibration and settings". The confirmation dialog already says this correctly (strings_settings2.xml:14).
    • Do the same in HI.
  • If skipped: this is a store-submission policy risk, and the in-app privacy claim becomes inaccurate as soon as ML Kit ships.

3. SM1 ships on by default with a haptic tick, but TESTING.md has no SM1 device checklist, so the condition the design relies on can't be met: docs/ARCHITECTURE-v2.md:506, :508; docs/TESTING.md (no SM1 section; §20 is Builder B's only); app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/smart/HandsFree.kt:91-101.

  • Problem:
    • ARCH's as-built note makes the haptic conditional: "device checklist item confirms tracking is unaffected, otherwise drop the tick" (ARCHITECTURE-v2.md:508). ARCH §5.6 also lists the device checks "hands-free on a shaky hold (tune holdMs); TalkBack announces".
    • None of this is in TESTING.md: a search for dwell, hands-free, haptic or ML Kit finds only §20 item 20 and the G2 item 22. Only that file is the release gate.
    • The research says Android uses sound cues because of the ARCore haptics caveat (docs/research/ui-ux.md §6.1 and §2.1), and SceneView's VIBRATE is stripped for that reason (AndroidManifest.xml:22-28). The deviation is recorded, but nothing verifies it.
    • On-by-default is a deviation that changes every existing user's Measure, Scan, Furniture and Calibrate flows.
  • Scenario:
    1. The RC goes to testers, who follow TESTING §1–§20.
    2. Nobody checks whether the tick shifts anchors right after the last point. PointAdded(complete = true) fires the tick while the result card's reading is still live-refined from anchors (MeasureSession.kt:415-425).
    3. Nobody checks whether 700 ms, 0.20 rad/s and 0.10 m/s suit a shaky hand or drop too eagerly for a steady one.
    4. Nobody checks whether the first TalkBack "Placed point 1" is spoken (MINOR 3).
    5. Nobody checks the ML Kit chip with the model present and absent, or that no MlKitInitProvider remains in the merged manifest.
  • Fix: add "§21 Smart Measure SM1" to TESTING.md. It should cover:
    • Tracking stability with the tick: a bench distance measured 5× hands-free vs 5× with "+", with the reading after 10 s; drop the tick if the hands-free spread is worse.
    • Dwell tuning: a shaky hold, a steady hold, and an existing user who keeps tapping "+" (MINOR 2).
    • Behaviour around overlays: no drop during the calibration picker, a freeze, or a dialog.
    • TalkBack: every drop is announced, including after an Undo.
    • ML Kit chip: on a fresh install before the model download (no chip), with the model (a chip within 3 s, EN and HI), and in airplane mode.
    • Merged-manifest check: no MlKitInitProvider, and no new permission.
    • Cold start: an am start -W comparison against 13f3740.
  • If skipped: an on-by-default behaviour change, and a haptic the research advises against, reach users with no device evidence. The ARCH condition "otherwise drop the tick" can never fire.

MINOR

4. There is no hold-off after a Freeze ends, so a point can drop at the spot the user just corrected away from: ar/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/ar/HandsFreeDropper.kt:63-67; MeasureSession.kt:658-680.

  • Problem: the dropper holds off only on a decrease in the point count, on a resume and on a toggle. While frozen, autoDropTarget() is null (MeasureSession.kt:498), but endFreeze doesn't change the count, so no hold-off follows. The re-arm spot is set only by a hands-free drop.
  • Scenario:
    1. The user taps "+" at X (manual), freezes, drags point 1 by 4 cm to X′, taps Done, and keeps the phone still (it is still aimed at X).
    2. 0.7 s later point 2 drops at X, 4 cm from X′, and a 4 cm distance completes.
  • Fix: have MeasureSession expose a freezeGeneration, or emit an event on endFreeze, and call trigger.holdOff() and set rearmFrom to the reticle target when it changes. Alternatively, have the dropper treat "frozen → live" as a hold-off edge.
  • If skipped: an occasional junk point after a freeze, which the user fixes with Undo.

5. "+" and the dwell compete for existing users: MeasureSession.kt:711-713; MeasureHud.kt:389-392; ResultCards.kt:174-187.

  • Problem: the "+" button is disabled only while pendingCommit is true, which lasts about one frame after an auto-drop. A user who aims, waits and taps "+" (aim to drop is about 1.2 s) taps just after the dwell has committed.
  • Scenario:
    • Point 1: the tap requests a second commit at the same spot, which is rejected as SAME_SPOT with the "same spot" message, an error shown for doing what the app taught them.
    • Last point: for the one to two frames before the worker publishes the non-live reading, "+" is still shown with isComplete = true. A tap then reaches addPoint(), whose first line clear()s a complete measurement (MeasureSession.kt:480). After those frames, the same finger lands on the result card's bottom row (Undo / New / Save).
  • Fix:
    • In addPoint(), ignore a manual tap within the dwell cool-down (about 1 s) of an auto-drop when the reticle target is within MIN_SPACING_M of that drop. Treat it as a confirmation (no error) rather than a new point.
    • Also guard addPoint()'s clear()-when-complete branch with "not within 1 s of completion".
    • Add a device check under MAJOR 3.
  • If skipped: confusing errors for upgrading users, and a rare lost result.

6. Hands-free and naming status isn't reliably announced: app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/smart/HandsFree.kt:100, :108-114; ScanReviewScreen.kt (the SuggestionChip).

  • Problem: the announcer is a 1 dp live-region node whose text is "Placed point N".
    • After Undo, the re-dropped point has the same N, so the semantics don't change and TalkBack says nothing.
    • The node is created on the first drop (if (n <= 0) return). Whether Compose announces a live region that appears, rather than one that changes, is device-dependent. Not verified.
    • The ML Kit chip appears up to 3 s after the photo, with no announcement.
  • Scenario:
    • A TalkBack user drops point 2, hears it, taps Undo, and holds again. Point 2 drops silently.
    • A TalkBack user never learns that a name suggestion exists.
  • Fix:
    • Keep the announcer node always composed with empty text.
    • Make the announced state a (count, sequence) pair so every drop changes the text, or call view.announceForAccessibility from the event collector.
    • Give the chip's row liveRegion = Polite, or announce once when nameSuggestion becomes non-null.

7. Live-region chatter from the readout: app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/measure/MeasureHud.kt:324-357; LiveAnnouncement.kt:138-139.

  • Problem: the throttled node includes the distance-to-target pill. The distance changes with every hand movement, so TalkBack gets a polite announcement every ≤ 2 s for the whole time the user is aiming, including before any point exists. These queue with the hint area, the step pill and "Placed point N".
  • Scenario: with TalkBack on, the user aims at a wall for 10 s and hears 5 distance readouts. The hands-free "Placed point 1" is delayed behind them, or cut off.
  • Fix:
    • Announce the distance only on a change of more than 10 cm, or not at all while there are 0 points.
    • Announce the live length only when the reading settles (SETTLE only, no 2 s forced gap) while a point is being aimed.
    • Leave the distance for touch exploration.

8. SpokenText gaps (EN and HI): app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/common/SpokenText.kt:46-80; strings_smart.xml:60-64.

  • Fractions: fractional inches pass through as raw text ("23 5/8 inches"; Units.kt:20, :287), so TTS decides how to read "5/8". Google TTS can read a slash pair as a date or as "five slash eight", and HI TTS is less predictable.
  • Units after 1: units are always plural: "1 inches" and "1 feet" (asserted by SpokenTextTest: "plus or minus 1 inches", "about 1 inches").
  • EN action labels: the new custom-action labels say "Move point 1 cm left" and the photo description says "1 cm at a time". These are exactly the symbols the M5 pass removes elsewhere; the HI strings are correct.
  • Scenario: an imperial user hears "twenty-three, May eighth, inches" on a frame width.
  • Fix:
    • Speak fractions in words through string resources ("23 and 5 eighths inches"; "5/8" → a11y_fraction_eighths, and so on for /16, /4, /2).
    • Choose singular or plural units with <plurals> keyed on the integer part.
    • Write "centimetre" in the EN action strings.
    • Add the tests.

9. Per-call regex compilation in SpokenText on hot UI paths: SpokenText.kt:49-57.

  • Problem: each speak() call builds a Map and compiles two Regexes ((\d)(mm|cm|m|in|ft)\b and \s+).
    • LiveReadout calls it on every recomposition (up to 10 Hz, one or two calls).
    • FreezeOverlay calls it on every drag frame for rectangle and box readings (up to 60 Hz), whether or not TalkBack is on.
  • Scenario: dragging a frozen box point causes about 120 regex compilations per second plus the token lists. That is GC churn on a mid-range phone during a precision drag.
  • Fix:
    • Hoist both regexes and the symbol map to private vals on the object, building the map from Words once per Words instance (or keying it by the words).
    • Optionally skip the work when AccessibilityManager.isTouchExplorationEnabled is false.

10. The new UMP retry in onStart can open the consent form over an AR screen, and hands-free keeps dropping behind it: app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/MainActivity.kt:45-50; AdsManager.kt:159-163, :190-201.

  • Problem: before this change the consent request was retried only "with the next activity", which never happened in this single-activity app. Now every onStart calls gatherConsent. That shows UMP's form, a dialog over the current activity, on whatever screen is in front, including Measure, Scan or Place. A dialog doesn't pause the activity, so the AR session (and the dwell, MAJOR 1's class) keeps running behind it.
    • The retry itself is idempotent: consentRequested and sdkStarted are CAS-guarded.
    • It is a no-op for Pro: adsAllowed starts false.
    • No ad request precedes consent: startSdkIfAllowed checks canRequestAds().
  • Scenario:
    1. First launch is offline, so the consent request fails.
    2. Later the user is measuring, switches to WhatsApp and comes back online. The consent form appears over the camera mid-task.
  • Fix: in onStart, retry only when !ads.arInForeground. Alternatively, move the retry into onNonArScreenResumed, the natural break that ui-ux §5.1 asks for.

11. Delete my data empties the whole cache directory, including third-party SDK caches, while the Settings banner's WebView is live: app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/settings/UserDataEraser.kt:63-68; AppContainer.kt:193.

  • Problem: the app's own cache content is cache/share/ and cache/place/ (GalleryRepository.kt:849, :669), and GalleryRepository.deleteAll already removes both (:457). clearCaches() additionally deletes everything else under cacheDir and externalCacheDir: the Chromium WebView HTTP and code caches, and whatever Play services and ML Kit keep there. It does this while Settings is composing an AdMob BannerAd.
  • Scenario: the user taps Delete everything on Settings with a banner showing. The WebView's disk cache disappears under a running Chromium network service.
    • The usual result is cache misses and logged errors, not a crash. But this isn't user data, and "caches" fails whenever an SDK holds a directory it recreates, so the row shows "partial" with no way to fix it.
  • Fix: drop the cacheDirs step, or limit it to app-owned subdirectories. The share and place directories are already covered.
  • If skipped: a spurious "Some data could not be deleted" result and SDK cache churn. No user data is affected either way.

12. ML Kit's failure modes are silent: app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/smart/MlKitObjectNamer.kt:27, :41-45; ObjectNamer.kt:60-66.

  • sdkinternal reliance: MlKitContext.initializeIfNeeded is a @KeepForSdk API in com.google.mlkit.common.sdkinternal, not public API.
    • A rename or signature change breaks the build on the next version bump. That is visible and acceptable.
    • A semantic change breaks only at runtime, for example a new component the removed MlKitInitProvider used to register. The exception is swallowed by LabelObjectNamer (catch (e: Exception) { null }), so the chip silently never appears again.
  • Cancellation: addOnCanceledListener { cont.cancel() } resumes the caller with a CancellationException, which LabelObjectNamer rethrows as though the caller were cancelled (:62-63). That contradicts "Never throws". It is harmless only because ScanViewModel.suggestName launches a throwaway job.
  • No cancellation hook: there is no invokeOnCancellation, so a task that never completes keeps the labeller open and the bitmap referenced. This is documented and bounded per photo.
  • Scenario:
    • After a dependency bump, the naming chip disappears for every user and nobody notices.
    • A Play-services-side cancel ends the naming job with a cancellation instead of null.
  • Fix:
    • Map a task cancellation to resumeWithException(IOException(...)), or resume(emptyList()).
    • Log a WARN once per process when labels() throws: the class name only, no PII.
    • Add the MAJOR 3 device check ("chip appears with the model present") to catch a silent regression on each ML Kit bump.
    • Pin the ML Kit version in libs.versions.toml with a comment that bumping it requires that device check.

13. The store-build guard checks only that the values are present, but AppLinks silently rejects malformed ones: app/build.gradle.kts:58-59 (pre-existing guard); app/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/about/AppLinks.kt:22-27.

  • Problem: the guard passes any non-blank PRIVACY_POLICY_URL or SUPPORT_EMAIL. At runtime, AppLinks.privacyPolicyUrl accepts only https://, and supportEmail must pass isPlausibleEmail; otherwise they are null and Settings and About show no policy link.
  • Scenario: the CI secret holds http://spaceview.example/privacy, or an address with a stray space. The store build succeeds, and the shipped app has no privacy-policy link, which Play requires for apps with ads.
  • Fix: apply the same two checks in the Gradle guard (https prefix, and the same email rule) and fail the store build otherwise.

14. Help still teaches "tap +" and never mentions hands-free, although it is now on by default: app/src/main/res/values/strings_help.xml:11, :20 (and HI).

  • Scenario: a user wonders why points appear by themselves. Help → "Hold steady when you add a point" says nothing about the dwell or where to switch it off.
  • Fix: add a "Hands-free points" FAQ entry: what it does, the HUD switch, the Settings switch, and that Undo is one tap away. Mention it in the accuracy section as well. EN and HI.

15. G2: reflections of furniture can form a strong 2-D "floor" below a tracked floor plane: ar/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/ar/FloorEstimator.kt:124-167; docs/TESTING.md:305-307.

  • Problem: the new strong() test (≥ 30 hits, minor-axis σ ≥ 0.10 m, ≥ 2 s) lets a point-only bin below a plane win. On a mirror-polished floor, the reflection of a table top or bed is a horizontal 2-D patch at minus its height. It is seen over time, so it passes all three criteria wherever hits fall outside the floor plane's polygon. The old rule ("a plane always wins") prevented exactly this, at the cost of G2.
  • Scenario: on a marble floor that ARCore does track, with a 75 cm table reflected near the plane's edge, the floor jumps 75 cm down. Wall–floor taps are then rejected, and the wall centre-height readout is wrong.
  • Fix:
    • Extend device item 22 with "polished floor that ARCore does track, a table reflected in it".
    • In code, consider requiring the strong bin to be within about 0.30 m below the plane (a table's underside never reflects that close), or requiring onPlane hits to be absent in the strong bin's x–z footprint.

16. There is no test for the session-side contract the dwell depends on: ar/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/ar/MeasureSession.kt:497-502; HandsFreeDropper.kt:63-82.

  • Problem: DwellTriggerTest covers the pure trigger well (10 cases, including repeated timestamps and a clock restart). The rules "no target while frozen, complete, + pending or unanchored" and "hold-off on a count decrease" live in autoDropTarget() and HandsFreeDropper.onFrame, which no test covers.
  • Scenario: a later edit to autoDropTarget() drops the commitRequestedAtMs >= 0 clause, and the dwell double-commits over a pending "+". Nothing fails.
  • Fix:
    • Extract the predicate autoDropAllowed(closed, live, frozen, freezeRequested, pending, count, required, pointsOk) as a pure function and table-test it.
    • Test HandsFreeDropper's count-decrease hold-off with a fake session seam, or by moving that logic into DwellTrigger.onPointCount(n).

Answers to the brief's focus questions

Dwell correctness

  • Unintended drops:
    • While frozen: no; autoDropTarget() is null when frozenCapture != null || freezeRequested (MeasureSession.kt:498). Right after a freeze: yes (MINOR 4).
    • After completion: no (endpoints.size >= requiredPoints → null, :499), so the dwell never reaches addPoint()'s clear-and-restart branch.
    • On resume: no. There is a 1 s hold-off (HandsFreeDropper.kt:54-56), and the incomplete points are cleared on pause (MeasureSession.kt:360-364).
    • Double drop: no. There is a 1 s cool-down plus re-arm after 3 cm (DwellTrigger.kt:130-133), and the commit is refused while one is pending (:498).
    • During calibration known-length: yes, through the hidden-picker path (MAJOR 1).
  • Does it fight "+"? In the commit logic, no: a pending "+" nulls the target, and a manual point blocks the same spot through nearestCommittedM. In the UX, yes (MINOR 5).
  • Thread safety:
    • Everything the dropper touches runs on the main thread: SceneView callbacks (ArFrameListener.kt:29), SideEffect for enabled, and _progress (a StateFlow).
    • The only cross-thread datum is the worker's @Volatile candidate, which is read once into a local (MeasureSession.kt:500).
    • No race found.
  • Haptic tick risk for tracking: plausible but unmeasured. The mitigations (after commit, inside the cool-down) protect new samples but not the live anchor refinement of the points already committed. This needs a device check (MAJOR 3).
  • Per-frame cost:
    • onFrame does O(points ≤ 4) work and no allocation; Float boxing in _progress happens only on the ≤ 5 step changes per hold.
    • The ring is read in a draw lambda (MeasureHud.kt:284), so it causes no recomposition per frame.
    • The announcement path is fine apart from MINOR 9.

ML Kit

  • Network: inference is on-device; Play services downloads the model at install (ica).
  • Telemetry: diagnostics go to Google, which the Data safety form must declare (MAJOR 2).
  • No new permission: this is the builder's claim. I did not check the merged manifest.
  • sdkinternal: acceptable with a device check per bump; it fails silently (MINOR 12).
  • Threading and cold start: nothing runs at cold start (the provider is removed). Init, decode and process start on Dispatchers.Default (ObjectNamer.kt:61); the task listeners run on main and only resume.
  • Timeout: withTimeoutOrNull correctly gives up waiting, and caller cancellation propagates. The cancel-listener edge case is MINOR 12.

UMP and ads

  • The ordering is unchanged: the SDK starts only when canRequestAds() allows.
  • The onStart re-call is idempotent and a no-op for Pro.
  • No ad loads before consent.
  • One UX edge (MINOR 10).

In-app review

  • Never on AR: arInForeground is checked first (ReviewPolicy.kt:70), and asks happen only from NonArScreenAdEffect.
  • Never after an interstitial: interstitialBusy covers the owed, deciding and showing states (AdsManager.kt:136), plus a quiet window of 10 minutes.
  • At most once per 90 days.
  • Clock rollback means "too soon" (ReviewPolicy.kt:76; the safe direction).
  • Each launch counts as an ask, and is recorded before launching.
  • Cold start: ReviewPrompter is built on Home's first composition, but it touches no I/O or Play API until an ask (PlayReviewLauncher.manager is lazy).

Delete my data

  • Complete for user content: Room History and Gallery rows, files/gallery/**, cache/share, cache/place, the measure DataStore, and the app settings except onboarding.
  • Excluded by design: the ad counters, the review record, the entitlement cache (Pro is unaffected) and UMP consent.
  • Partial failure: each step runs and reports its own flag; a retry is idempotent.
  • Process death: gallery rows deleted before the files are deleted leave orphan files, which cleanUp() removes on the next gallery open (GalleryRepository.kt:498-523). The other steps aren't resumable but are harmless to re-run.
  • 3D Scan Lab files (files/scan3d…, LabPerf.kt:109) aren't erased. That is debug-only and acceptable.
  • One overreach (MINOR 11). The wording issue is in MAJOR 2.

N2

  • A one-shot check that would say NeedsPro waits for settled or Pro, for at most 5 s, after the existing ≤ 1 s Unknown wait. The worst case is about 6 s, not the 5 s stated in HANDOFF (nit 1).
  • An "Allowed" answer never waits, so no sequence of checks stacks two waits:
    • checkDeviceScan: the first check either returns NeedsPro (no second check) or is Allowed without waiting. Worst case about 6 s, not 10 s. It also has no main-build caller today.
  • No UI blocks:
    • Home shows "Checking…" with a spinner and ignores repeat taps (AppNavHost.kt:99-115).
    • Gallery's scan button exists only in the empty state, where the gate always allows.
    • Furniture already shows "Checking…".

Accessibility

  • FreezeOverlay nudges are correct:
    • The probe and the move intersect the same plane through the last point (MeasureSession.kt:639-654), so restore() is exact.
    • Scaling 20 px to 1 cm adapts to perspective, and a refused probe changes nothing.
  • 48 dp targets are met on the new controls (the switch, the mode tabs, the chip, the dialog buttons, the nudge buttons).
  • Gaps: MINORs 6–8.

Strings

  • 688 keys, with full EN/HI parity across all eight strings*.xml pairs. Every key is in the same file in both locales, and placeholders match.
  • The only unused key, home_accuracy_good, is pre-existing.
  • The five keys removed from strings.xml (common_close, settings_version, settings_licences, settings_licences_apache, settings_contact) have no remaining references in either locale.

Merge correctness

The shared files compose correctly:

  • SettingsScreen carries both builders' parameters.
  • MeasureSettingsRepository has both setHandsFreeEnabled and clearAll, and clearAll resets hands-free to its default (on).
  • HomeScreen, AppNavHost, PlaceScreen and FurnitureMeasureScreen are each internally consistent.
  • ScanViewModel.settingsFlow feeds both Scan and Furniture, so both honour the setting.

Nits (not counted)

  1. HANDOFF says the N2 gate "waits up to 5 s". It is ≤ 1 s (Unknown) + ≤ 5 s (settle).
  2. ARCH §5.1 still says "MeasureSession itself is unchanged" above an as-built note that lists its new members. Strike the old line to avoid confusion.
  3. HomeScreen.kt and ScanRoute.kt put new imports above the existing block, out of order. Leave it to lint or ktlint.

Not checked:

  • Build, tests and lint: no Gradle build, unit test or lint run. HANDOFF records that lint wasn't re-run after A's last string change.
  • Merged release manifest: I did not check whether MlKitInitProvider is gone, whether ML Kit or Review add any permission, or the +158 KB size claim.
  • On a device: nothing was run, including:
    • the haptic and tracking interaction;
    • the dwell tuning;
    • the TalkBack behaviour of the appearing live region, fractions and Hindi TTS;
    • the UMP form on an EEA test device;
    • the Play review card on an internal track;
    • cold-start timings.
  • The current text of Google's ML Kit and Play Billing data-disclosure pages: I cited them from ARCH and memory, not fetched.
  • Excluded from the read:
    • the Help and About content beyond the privacy and hands-free strings;
    • the full text of ContrastTokensTest's 19 pairs (I didn't recompute the ratios);
    • OssLicences completeness beyond spot-checking the ML Kit, Review and Firebase rows;
    • AdsConsentTest and AdsReviewHandOffTest bodies (only their names and the code they cover);
    • Builder B's a11y edits in GalleryItemScreen, GalleryScreen, HistoryScreen, PaywallScreen, OnboardingScreen, AccuracyBadge, DimensionLabel, ArGate and FurnitureScreens, beyond the diff stat (only the SpokenText call pattern was checked).

T + D0 gate: furniture templates, 3D Scan Lab spike harness, N1/N3/N4/N5 (Final Reviewer + Judge)

FRIDAY, 2026-11-17. Gate tree: the uncommitted work on top of de63706. It covers:

  • T: furniture templates (Builder B), with the MINOR 4 fix round (TemplateGoldenTest, per-template constants objects);
  • D step 1: the debug-only 3D Scan Lab spike harness, plus carry-over MINORs N1, N3, N4 and N5 (Builder A), with the B1 / M2 / MINOR 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 fix round.

I checked it against HANDOFF.md (Phase 2 entries), docs/ARCHITECTURE-v2.md §4.3, §4.5, §6 (with the new immutability rule), §7.1.6 (updated governor rule), §7.1.10, docs/reviews/M4-P1-gate.md §8 and docs/reviews/T-D0-review.md. No source was edited and no Gradle task was run; this file is the only write.

Verdict: PASS WITH CONDITIONS

T is APPROVED. All six gate §8 T requirements hold, and review MINOR 4 is closed by a 39-case golden test.

D step 1 is APPROVED for the spike, after one fix. BLOCKER 1 and MAJOR 2 are fixed in the code, and each has a test that fails on the old code. The fixes introduce no new BLOCKER or MAJOR. However, I found one MAJOR the review missed (G1), which is pre-existing in the harness rather than a regression:

  • The problem: the lab's criterion-2 frame check, c2_ar_p95_le_33ms, compares Choreographer intervals against 33.0 ms. Those intervals are whole multiples of the vsync period, so a session holding a steady 30 fps reads 33.33 ms and is flagged FAIL. This is the same trap as BLOCKER 1, moved from the governor to the metrics.
  • What survives: the raw ar_frame_ms_p95 is logged, so no data is lost.
  • The risk: the flag would push the spike towards the "if 2 fails" branch for no reason. It is a two-constant fix plus one test (R1), and it must land before the spike APK is built.

Decision on the orchestrator's call (debug build for the spike): upheld, with a rule.

  • Conclusive from a debug build: criterion 1 + R2 (accuracy), and any PASS of criteria 2–4.
  • Not conclusive: a FAIL of fusion time, AR frame time, thermal or processing time. Each of those must be re-run on a release-signed lab build before anyone acts on it (§4).

There are three conditions (§6): R1 is code and R2 is documentation, both small, and R3 is the APK hand-off.

How this was verified

1. BLOCKER and MAJOR from the review

# Finding Status Evidence
B1 The governor's 33.0 ms frame rule fired on every 30 fps session, so integration fell to 2 Hz FIXED Rule: ShapeScanGovernor.kt:93 steps down only when the p90 of the camera intervals is above dropThresholdNs = framePeriodNs × DROP_FACTOR (1.5) (:34, :169), which is 50 ms at 30 fps. The period defaults to FRAME_PERIOD_30FPS_NS = 33,333,333 (:166) and is set from the session's camera config before capture (DepthCaptureListener.kt:192-194). Healthy case: governorStaysAt5HzOnAHealthy30fpsCamera (ShapeScanCaptureTest.kt:33) feeds 90 s of 33.33 ms ± 1 ms intervals with a 2.5% rate of single drops, and asserts 5 Hz with 0 events. The old 33.0 ms rule fails it, because every p90 is about 34 ms. Real drop: governorStepsDownOnDroppedFramesWithACooldownAndNeverStepsUp (:47). A 200 ms hiccup keeps 5 Hz; alternating 33.3 / 66.7 ms intervals (p90 66.7 ms) step down to 3 Hz, then to 2 Hz after the 2 s cooldown; healthy frames never step back up. 60 fps: governorDropThresholdFollowsTheCameraRate (:67) gives a 25 ms threshold. Spec: ARCH §7.1.6 now states the 1.5× rule.
M2 Processing PSS left out the volume (an under-count of up to 12.6 MB) FIXED Formula: LabMetrics.kt:192-194 computes the processing extra as (stage peak − processing baseline) + volumeBytes, and peak_extra_pss_mb is the larger of capture and processing (:197). Baseline: taken after the AR screen has gone, by settledPss() (LabViewModel.kt:264, :300-310): two readings 500 ms apart within 1 MB, after at least 1 s and at most about 4 s. No caller-frame volume local: steps 1–2 moved into noiseAndMesh (ShapeScanPipeline.kt:167-179), which sets holder.volume = null before returning. process holds only noise, coverage, voxelM and the mesh. Test: processingExtraCountsTheVolumeHeldInItsBaseline (LabMetricsTest.kt:140) has a 12.4 MB volume plus 30 MB of meshing. It expects 41.83 MB in pss_extra_processing_incl_volume_mb, and c3_extra_pss_le_40mb = false. The old formula gives max(24.4, 30) = 30 MB, which passes, so the test fails on the old code. Order D2 is unchanged: noise → marching cubes → release → floor clip → components → decimate → extent → GLB.

The pending start then sees capture !== c (:215), and FrameIntervalRecorder.start clears even while running (LabPerf.kt:27-33). Code-verified only.

3. New issues

One MAJOR (G1) that the review missed, plus MINORs. G1 is pre-existing in the D0 harness; G2 to G4 come from, or sit next to, the fixes.

G1. MAJOR: the criterion-2 frame check fails a steady 30 fps session: LabMetrics.kt:137, :236; LabViewModel.kt:481 (JANK_NS).

  • Problem:
    • ar_frame_ms_* are Choreographer frameTimeNanos intervals (LabPerf.kt:41-45). Those are whole multiples of the vsync period: 16.67, 33.33 or 50 ms on a 60 Hz panel, and 8.33, 16.67, 25 or 33.33 ms on a 120 Hz one.
    • c2_ar_p95_le_33ms tests p95 ≤ 33.0, so one missed vsync in more than 5% of frames reads 33.33 ms → FAIL. In effect the check demands about 60 fps (or about 40 fps on a 120 Hz panel). Criterion 2 is "30 fps AR", and its gfxinfo reference measures frame duration, not the interval.
    • JANK_NS = 33_000_000 counts every 30 Hz frame as janky in the same way.
    • The test input choreographerMs = Quantiles(16.7, 30.1, …) (LabMetricsTest.kt:33) uses a p95 that Choreographer cannot produce. That is the same blind spot as B1's 33 ms test input.
  • Scenario:
    • A mid-range phone runs the lab on debug. SceneView, MeasureSession and the capture copy-out take 17–30 ms of main-thread work per frame, so the screen holds a steady 30 fps.
    • ar_frame_ms_p95 = 33.333 and c2_ar_p95_le_33ms = false, and the result screen lists it as false.
    • Per the orchestrator's rule, a debug c2 FAIL triggers the release-signed lab build. That build may hold 30 fps too and still read "false", which leads to the §7.1.10 "If 2 fails → lower N_MAX and the rate" branch with nothing wrong.
  • Fix (smallest correct change):
    • Set MAX_AR_P95_MS = 1000.0 / 30 + 0.5 (33.83) and JANK_NS = 33_833_333L.
    • With that, an exact 30 Hz cadence passes, and a missed 30 Hz slot fails (41.7 ms at 120 Hz, 44.4 ms at 90 Hz, 50 ms at 60 Hz).
    • Add a LabMetricsTest case: p95 = 33.333 gives true, and p95 = 50.0 gives false.
    • Don't rename the column. Note the definition in the KDoc.
  • If skipped: the go/no-go for criterion 2 is decided on a flag that fails healthy phones. The raw p95 is still in the CSV, so the damage can be undone by hand, but only if someone notices.
# Severity Where Problem and scenario Fix
G2 MINOR (regression of the MINOR 3 fix) FloorEstimator.kt:96-97 Problem: "any plane bin wins wherever it is" also lets a higher plane beat a real point-backed floor below it. Scenario: a glossy plain vitrified floor that ARCore never turns into a plane, with a textured coffee table that it does. Depth and point hits on the floor qualify (≥ 5 hits, ≥ 15 cm spread), but the table plane at +0.45 m is the floor. Every wall–floor tap is then rejected by verticalThroughFloorLine, and the wall centre-height reads 45 cm low (PlacementCore.kt:321, 405). Context: the old rule handled this case and failed MINOR 3's mirrored-floor case; the new one is the reverse. Height alone cannot tell the two apart, and which one happens on real floors is a device question. Decide from device item 22 (§7) before the M6 polish. Candidate fix: a point-only bin below the lowest plane may still win when its spread is ≥ 0.5 m in both x and z, because a floor patch is 2-D while a mirrored edge is a line. Add a test for each case.
G3 MINOR LabViewModel.kt:299-310 Problem: settledPss() gives up after about 4 s (1 s + 6 × 500 ms, plus the Debug.getPss calls, about 0.1–0.5 s on a low-end phone) and returns the last reading whether or not it settled. No column says which. Scenario: on a slow phone the camera and Filament teardown is still releasing memory when the baseline is read. The stage PSS readings then fall below the baseline, and the processing extra under-reports. That is the M2 direction, though bounded. Not affected: processing_ms, which sums stage times taken outside the probe (ShapeScanPipeline.kt:107-109). Analysis rule now (no rebuild): in metrics.json, the noise stage's pss_mb should be ≥ the processing baseline − 1 MB. If it is lower, PSS was still falling, so discard that run's c3 and re-run. Optional append while R1 is open: pss_settle_ms and pss_settled.
G4 MINOR DepthCaptureListener.kt:192-194 Problem: the drop threshold comes from fpsRange.upper, and the range is not logged. (a) A 60 fps config (reachable only if the TARGET_FPS_30 filter falls back to session.cameraConfig) gives 25 ms. An app rendering a steady 30 Hz would then step down for FRAME_TIME while AR meets its 30 fps budget. (b) A variable range such as [15, 30] (whether ARCore reports one is unverified): in dim light, auto-exposure halves the camera rate, which gives FRAME_TIME step-downs that are not app load. Use framePeriodNs = max(1e9 / upper, FRAME_PERIOD_30FPS_NS), since the governor protects the 30 fps AR budget. Append camera_fps_min and camera_fps_max. Analysis rule now: a FRAME_TIME event with a healthy ar_frame_ms_p95 and camera_frame_ms_p95 ≈ 66 ms means a camera-side drop (light), not app load. Don't count it against criterion 2; re-run in better light.
G5 NIT LabMetrics.kt:106-133, :278 Positions: the 104 original columns are untouched and 8 are appended, as required (112 now). Meanings: three existing columns changed meaning in place: c2_rate_ge_3hz (now the governor rate), peak_extra_pss_mb (now includes the volume), and c3_no_severe (can be "unknown"). This is safe today: the header changed, so LabStore.save rotates the old runs.csv (LabPerf.kt:123-127), and no lab build has left the team. But: nothing pins the header, and the JSON still says "schema": 1. Pin the first 104 names in a literal golden list in LabMetricsTest, and bump the JSON to "schema": 2. Can ride with R1.
G6 DOC ARCH §7.1.10, §7.1.6, §4.3, §6.2 §7.1.10 says "release build", but the orchestrator's decision (HANDOFF) is debug, plus the lab build on a timing FAIL. §7.1.6 says "a 1-slot channel with DROP_OLDEST"; the code has 2 pooled slots, trySend, and a backlog step-down. §4.3 Allowance lacks Only. §6.2 says "Gallery FAB → Add furniture"; the build has the Home row plus the empty-gallery button (review N-c). → R2.

Answers to the specific checks:

  • Governor framePeriodNs:
    • At 30 fps (the normal case, given SessionSetup.kt:41) the threshold is correct: 50 ms.
    • At 60 it is too strict for a 30 Hz renderer, and with a variable range it misattributes exposure drops.
    • Both are G4, and both are unlikely under the TARGET_FPS_30 filter.
    • Robust in either case: the 128-entry ring holds the 2 s window up to 60 fps, and MIN_SAMPLES = 20. One drop in fewer than 10% of frames never trips the p90.
  • The PSS settle loop on slow devices: it is bounded (about 4–5 s added before processing) and never affects processing_ms. The risk is an unsettled baseline that under-reports; detect it with G3's rule.
  • CSV append-only: by position, yes. By meaning, three columns changed, which is mitigated by rotation (G5).
  • Volume lifetime on debug: noiseAndMesh removes the caller-frame local. The startCapture coroutine's vol dies with the coroutine, because there is no suspension after c.start. finish() nulls the listener's reference. The only remaining holder is VolumeHolder, which is cleared at ShapeScanPipeline.kt:177.

Checked and clean:

  • Governor time base: onFrame, onBacklog and onThermal all use the capture's clockNs, and meanRateHz integrates over the same base (LabViewModel.kt:373).
  • SEVERE in the mean rate: it records rate 0 after the stop.
  • observedFraction: O(1) (TsdfVolume.kt:293), so it doesn't lengthen the worker's slot hold.
  • Lab debug app:
    • It installs beside the release app (applicationIdSuffix = ".debug", build.gradle.kts:107), so the user's M4 gallery is untouched.
    • FileProvider uses ${applicationId}.fileprovider (AndroidManifest.xml:89), which matches LabStore.
    • Debug sells through FakeBilling.

4. Spike readiness

Can the user run §7.1.10 and bring back valid data? Yes, once R1 is in the APK and the analysis rules below are followed.

The data is there:

  • Criterion 1 and R2: the labels carton-0.7m and carton-1.5m, typed tape W/H/D, mesh_minus_tape_*, mesh_pm_covers_tape, and the actual stand-off in mean_range_m (use it, not the label, for R2's error-versus-range check). aspect_mismatch covers MINOR 7.
  • Criterion 2: fusion_ms_p95, ar_frame_ms_p95, governor_mean_hz, governor_final_hz and governor_events.
  • Criterion 3: thermal_*, peak_extra_pss_mb and the per-stage PSS in the JSON.
  • Criterion 4: processing_ms and the per-stage times.

The protocol text in the lab (strings_scan3d.xml:8) matches §7.1.10 plus R2.

What a debug build can and cannot conclude

A debuggable runtime JITs with fewer optimisations, has no AOT or baseline profile, and keeps locals alive to the end of each method. That makes CPU-bound work slower and memory lifetimes longer, but leaves array sizes and the ARCore and VIO data the same.

Criterion Columns Debug PASS Debug FAIL
1 + R2: accuracy c1_mesh_within_pm_of_box, mesh_minus_tape_*, mean_range_m Conclusive Conclusive if the run integrated normally (no BACKLOG event, governor_final_hz ≥ 3). If a debug-only backlog starved it of frames, re-run on lab. Before blaming depth, check aspect_mismatch.
2: fusion c2_fusion_le_15ms Conclusive (release is faster) Not conclusive: re-run on lab.
2: AR frame time at ≥ 3 Hz c2_ar_p95_le_33ms (after R1), c2_rate_ge_3hz, governor_final_hz Conclusive only if c2_rate_ge_3hz = true and there is no BACKLOG event; otherwise the pass was bought by a lower rate Not conclusive: re-run on lab.
3: thermal c3_no_severe (unknown below API 29) Conclusive (debug burns more CPU) Not conclusive: re-run on lab.
3: memory c3_extra_pss_le_40mb, pss_extra_processing_incl_volume_mb Conclusive if G3's settle check passes. Debug over-counts: the whole volume is added back, plus JIT cache growth and longer local lifetimes. Probably real, but re-run on lab before lowering N_MAX.
4: processing c4_processing_le_5s Conclusive Not conclusive: re-run on lab.

When a release-signed lab build is required:

  1. Before acting on any FAIL of the criterion-2, criterion-3 or criterion-4 rows above, and in particular before taking the §7.1.10 "If 2 or 3 fail" branch (lower N_MAX and the rate, or open the GLES-compute ADR).
  2. Always, before D's user-facing timing promises ship. That covers the ≤ 3 s processing target with its progress bar, and the 30 fps capture claim. The Phase 3 release candidate re-measures criteria 2 and 4 on the release build itself (§8, P3-4).

Building the lab build type when it is needed:

  • Build type:
    • create("lab") { initWith(getByName("release")); applicationIdSuffix = ".lab"; versionNameSuffix = "-lab"; signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName("debug"); matchingFallbacks += "release" }
    • The sourceSets["lab"] source set points at src/debug/kotlin, src/debug/res and src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml. Today src/debug holds only the lab.
  • Entry point: add buildConfigField("boolean", "LAB", …) (true for lab, false for the others), and gate the Settings link on BuildConfig.DEBUG || BuildConfig.LAB.
    • The link is needed because the activity is not exported, so adb am start cannot reach it on a non-debuggable build.
  • Profiling: add <profileable android:shell="true"/> in the lab manifest so gfxinfo and Perfetto work.
  • Release safety: never upload lab. CI keeps checking that the release dex has 0 scan3d_lab (R3).
  • Telling builds apart: the -lab suffix shows in the app_version column, so lab rows and debug rows stay separate.

7. Device checklist for docs/TESTING.md §19 (T templates + the 3D Scan Lab spike)

T: Furniture templates (release or debug app; Free first, then Pro through FakeBilling on debug or a licence tester on release)

  1. Entry:
    • Home → Furniture opens the picker.
    • An empty gallery shows "Add furniture".
    • A non-empty gallery has no furniture entry (known, N-c).
  2. Free versus Pro templates:
    • On Free, sofa, bed and wardrobe start.
    • L-sofa, dining table, dining chair, TV unit, bookshelf and study table open the paywall before any camera.
    • On Pro, all nine start.
  3. Guided measure:
    • Each W/D/H Measure opens a one-shot AR measure and returns its value with ±.
    • Type enters an exact value with no ±.
    • Untouched defaults show "typical".
    • Save stays disabled until W, H and D are each measured or typed.
    • Invalid values (seat above the height, for example) show an inline error.
  4. Preview:
    • The 3D preview follows the options: seats, doors, shelves, chaise side.
    • The L-sofa's left and right are mirror images.
    • The overall size matches the entered W×H×D.
  5. Review and Save:
    • Review shows the "overall box" note. Save → Saved.
    • Placing the item stands it on the floor with a W×D footprint.
    • Next to the real sofa or bed, the outline matches within the item's ±.
  6. Verdict: an L-sofa against a measured gap says "Checked against the overall box (width × depth × height)".
  7. Gallery cap:
    • On Free with 20 items, the picker opens the paywall before AR.
    • At 19 items, start a template, then make the account lapse (FakeBilling) before Save. Save shows the needs-Pro card and keeps the draft. After upgrading, Save works.
  8. Process death (Developer options → "Don't keep activities"):
    • Background the app mid-measure, at Review and at Saved.
    • Step, values (with ±), options, preset, palette and name are restored. Saved does not save twice.
  9. Stability: a saved template looks identical after an app restart and after placing it twice.
  10. Lapse never hides data (ADR-005 rule 2): save an L-sofa as Pro, then lapse. It still opens, places, shares and deletes.
  11. Ads:
    • Save → Saved → Done: at most one ad, and only on a non-AR screen.
    • Saved → Place → Back: no ad.
    • Never an ad over the camera.

    • The picker, guided measure and Review are in Hindi with nothing truncated.
    • TalkBack reads each parameter row, with its value and source.
    • Targets are ≥ 48 dp.

3D Scan Lab spike (debug APK builds/SpaceView-TD0-debug.apk from R3: package com.spaceview.app.debug, which installs beside the release app; depth phone)

  1. Setup:
    • Install the APK, then open Settings → the debug panel → 3D Scan Lab.
    • Depth must show a source (RAW, HARDWARE or SMOOTHED). Note which.
    • Start each block cool, in good even light.
    • Tape the carton (about 60×40×40 cm) and type its W/H/D on the intro screen.
  2. Carton at about 0.7 m, 5 scans (label carton-0.7m):
    • Mark the box: 3 base corners, then the top.
    • Tap Start, walk slowly all the way round for 45–90 s, then Finish.
    • Record c1_mesh_within_pm_of_box and mesh_minus_tape_*.
  3. Carton at about 1.5 m, 5 scans (label carton-1.5m), with the same tape values (R2).
  4. Armchair, 5 scans, and a 2–3-seat sofa about 5 cm from a wall, 5 scans, each taped. Check:
    • there is no wall patch in the mesh viewer;
    • D is not inflated;
    • c4_processing_le_5s.
  5. One full 90 s scan from a cool start:
    • stop_reason = TIME_CAP;
    • record thermal_max and c3_no_severe;
    • record peak_extra_pss_mb.
  6. A second phone, ideally a smoothed-depth-only one: repeat items 14 and 15.
  7. Harness edge cases:
    • Back during "Starting…": the next run's numbers are clean (ar_frames is about 90 s worth, not doubled).
    • Start while the phone is hot: "too warm" is shown, with no dead capture.
    • App switch mid-capture: the capture stops with SESSION_PAUSED and processes what it captured.
  8. Save one sofa scan from the lab:
    • the item is ≤ 0.5 MB;
    • it places on the floor at the measured footprint (bottom about 1 cm up);
    • it shows in the debug app's gallery only.
  9. Share all results: send spaceview-scan3d-runs.csv, plus 2 or 3 metrics.json files and GLBs.
  10. Glossy floor (G2 and N1) (release app, Place):
    • On a polished vitrified or marble floor, do the plain-wall fallback twice: once with a coffee table in view, once without.
    • Note any wrongly rejected wall–floor taps and the centre-height readout.

How to read the CSV (orchestrator or FRIDAY; this goes into ARCH §7.1.10 under R2):

  • Valid run:
    • stop_reason is USER or TIME_CAP (a THERMAL_SEVERE run counts for criterion 3 only);
    • capture_s ≥ 45;
    • glb_error is empty.
  • Criterion 1: a set passes if 4 of 5 valid runs at one distance have c1_mesh_within_pm_of_box = true.
  • R2: plot mesh_minus_tape_* against mean_range_m. If the error grows with range beyond the ±, add the per-DepthSource range term.
  • Debug versus lab: apply the §4 table.
  • Camera-side drops (G4): a FRAME_TIME event with a healthy ar_frame_ms_p95 and camera_frame_ms_p95 ≈ 66 ms is a light problem, not app load.
  • Unsettled baseline (G3): if the JSON's noise stage pss_mb is below the processing baseline − 1 MB, ignore that run's c3.
  • Intrinsics before depth: aspect_mismatch = true combined with a c1 failure means check intrinsics before blaming depth.

8. Recommendations

D step 2: user-facing screens (only after the spike passes items 1–4 on at least one phone, or after the "ToF and raw only" / Beta decision)

  1. Reuse, don't copy. ShapeScanPipeline, DepthCaptureListener and ShapeScanGovernor are already in :ar main; build app/scan3d (main source set) on them. Never copy LabViewModel.save (MINOR 9).
  2. One gated store (D4): add saveMesh to GatedGalleryStore. Check checkDeviceScan() at scan entry before AR and again at Save, and keep the draft on NeedsPro. Record the completed scan for ads (K2), and add the D case to MeasureVisitTrackerTest (D7).
  3. Budget (D3): on a byte refusal, retry at 12k triangles, then offer "Save as box" from the kept box numbers. Never surface a raw IllegalArgumentException.
  4. Pause and process death (D8, §7.1.6): no TSDF checkpoint.
    • On resume, offer "Finish with what was captured" (≥ 50% coverage) or "Start again".
    • After process death in capture, show "The scan was interrupted", with Scan again and Save as box instead.
    • After process death in Review, restore the draft GLB and the crop values.
    • Cover each path with JVM tests on the view model. The lab's MINOR 5 and 8 fixes have no tests; the D view model must.
  5. Spec items the harness skipped on purpose:
    • "Colour integration is dropped first, before the rate" (§7.1.6). The lab always fuses colour, so its timings are conservative.
    • onTrimMemory(RUNNING_CRITICAL) → stop and offer Finish.
    • The typed ShapeScanError set, with the no-depth fallback to the box scan.
    • The 256 px WebP keyframe thumbnail (the lab saves none).
  6. Apply the spike results:
    • If R2 shows range-dependent error, add rangeBiasRel · r̄ per DepthSource before the mesh ± is shown.
    • Fix G4's clamp in the governor if R1 did not.
    • Tune N_MAX and the rates only from lab-build timing.
  7. Labels and gating (D9, D5):
    • Use "Approximate 3D shape · measured size" everywhere.
    • Ship as Beta until the bench holds on real depth.
    • Flip DEVICE_SCAN to shipped = true in the same change that adds the gated route.
    • Get the user's answer on "3 saved" versus "3 lifetime", and state it on the paywall.
  8. Keep the lab as a debug-only regression harness. Keep the CI release-dex check (R3).
  9. Hindi, TalkBack, 200% font on every D screen. No ads anywhere in the D flow until Saved.

T follow-ups (small, next fix pass)

  • T-1: in TemplateGoldenTest, also pin each id's static ParamSpec list (id, kind, min, max). A tightened optional range would then fail even when the 39 sampled maps don't hit it.
  • T-2: decide on the Gallery furniture entry (N-c): add the FAB per §6.2, or amend the spec (R2 records the deviation).

Phase 3: release candidate → Play internal track

  1. Release gate (§6.2): every BLOCKER and MAJOR is closed and verified in code, and CI is green on the RC commit. That covers tests, lint, Kover, the bundletool size gate (≤ 18 MiB; target ≤ 15 MB arm64), 16 KB alignment, and SpaceViewMigrationTest 3/3.
  2. Schema: v3 is closed (M4 shipped). Any schema change is v4, with a migration test from v1, v2 and v3, and an on-device install over M4.
  3. Device passes: TESTING §16–§19 end to end on one low-end and one mid-range phone, from a release-signed build installed over the previous one.
  4. If D ships in the RC: re-measure criteria 2 and 4 on that release build, never the debug or lab numbers. Run the 30 fps profile (gfxinfo, Perfetto; N5 GC check) on Place and on capture.
  5. Billing and policy:
    • Real Play Billing with licence testers (TESTING §17).
    • The Data safety form and the privacy policy match the app's behaviour (AdMob, UMP, no uploads).
    • The Firelog decision (P1-10).
  6. Accessibility: TalkBack, 200% font and contrast across Measure, Scan, Place, Furniture and Pro.
  7. Lint and polish (M6): the 6 app lint warnings (PluralsCandidate and UnusedResources from N7), the SceneView skybox and material strip (about 4 MB), and the EmojiCompat initializer.
  8. Hand-off artefacts:
    • An AAB from bundleRelease only, never lab.
    • Upload the R8 mapping, and keep the previous AAB.
    • The known-limitations list: L-sofa verdict on the overall box, an approximate 3D shape, depth-capable phones only, and the offline grace bound.
  9. Track: internal track first. A personal Play account then needs a closed test with 12 testers for 14 days before production (HANDOFF decision). Plan staged rollout and rollback.

Reviewsdocs/reviews/T-D0-review.md · updated 16 Nov 2026, 22:35

T + D0 review: furniture templates (Builder B) and the 3D-scan spike harness + N1/N3/N4/N5 (Builder A)

Reviewer: FRIDAY §1, §4.B (standard + thermonuclear), §4.E for the harness metrics. Read-only; this file is the only write. Scope: the uncommitted work on top of de63706 (git status, git diff HEAD, all untracked files listed there). Method: I read the tests first, then the diff, then the call sites (GalleryRepository save and placement paths, SessionSetup, TsdfVolume conventions, AdsManager visit API, GallerySaveGate, ReconMemoryTest). Evidence is file:line from this session. I ran no Gradle task (as instructed: the orchestrator's build is running and RAM is low). The only commands I ran were git and two read-only scripts: Hindi key parity, and placeholder parity across every strings*.xml in main and debug.

Verdict: FAIL for the spike run until BLOCKER 1 and MAJOR 2 are fixed. T is APPROVED WITH WARNINGS (MINORs only).

Counts: BLOCKER 1, MAJOR 1, MINOR 7. There are also 3 nits, which are not counted.

All findings are regressions in new code; none is a pre-existing defect. Both serious findings are in the spike harness and would corrupt the numbers the user brings back. Builder B's templates work is clean apart from MINORs.

BLOCKER

1. The governor's frame-time rule fires on every 30 fps session, so integration falls to 2 Hz within about 3 s: ar/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/ar/ShapeScanGovernor.kt:132 and :80, fed by DepthCaptureListener.kt:295.

  • Problem: The rule compares the p90 of camera-timestamp intervals against MAX_FRAME_P90_NS = 33_000_000. The camera is locked at 30 fps (SessionSetup.kt:41, TARGET_FPS_30), so the nominal interval is 33.33 ms. Even a perfect session has a p90 above 33.0 ms. The unit test feeds exactly 33 * ms (ShapeScanCaptureTest.kt, governorStepsDownOnSlowFramesButNotOnOneHiccupAndNeverStepsUp), so it passes on a value no real camera produces.
  • Scenario: The user starts a carton scan on any phone.
    1. After 20 intervals (about 0.7 s), the first evaluation steps the rate from 5 Hz to 3 Hz (FRAME_TIME).
    2. Two seconds later (the cooldown) it steps to 2 Hz, and the rate never steps back up.
  • Effect on the spike:
    • Criterion 2 ("p95 ≤ 33 ms at ≥ 3 Hz integration") can't be tested: c2_rate_ge_3hz is false on every run.
    • Criterion 1: a 90 s capture integrates at most about 180 frames instead of about 450, so coverage and the extents get worse.
    • Misleading cause: governor_events reads FRAME_TIME@700ms FRAME_TIME@2700ms, so the spike would blame frame time for a cost that isn't there. The likely conclusion would be "lower N_MAX and the rate" (§7.1.10's "If 2 or 3 fail" branch) when nothing is slow.
  • Fix (smallest correct change): Measure missed camera frames instead of the raw interval.
    • Step down when the p90 interval exceeds about 1.5× the nominal period. That is about 50 ms at 30 fps, meaning frames are being dropped.
    • Alternatively, use the wall-clock updateIntervalNs against the same 1.5× bound.
    • Name the constant relative to the locked fps.
    • Change the test to feed 33.4 ms intervals (with ±1 ms jitter) and assert no step-down, then feed 66.7 ms intervals (one frame dropped in two) and assert a step-down.
    • Correct ARCH §7.1.6's wording ("p90 exceeds 33 ms (from frame timestamps)") to match, because the spec carries the same trap.
  • If skipped: every spike run reports the wrong integration rate and a false frame-time cause, and the go/no-go decision for D is made on corrupted data.

MAJOR

2. Criterion 3's processing number leaves out the TSDF, so "peak extra PSS" under-reports by up to about 12.6 MB: app/src/debug/kotlin/com/spaceview/app/scan3d/LabViewModel.kt:241; LabMetrics.kt:177.

  • Problem:
    • processingBaseline is read after c.finish() but before the pipeline drops the volume. holder.volume is cleared only at ShapeScanPipeline.kt:123, so the baseline already contains the TSDF.
    • extraProcessing = peakProcessing − processingBaseline is therefore only the meshing working set on top of the volume.
    • The criterion, and the JVM bound it is meant to confirm, count the volume plus marching cubes together. ReconMemoryTest gives "marching cubes (volume alive) 18.9 MB = volBytes + aMc".
    • peak_extra_pss_mb = max(extraCapture, extraProcessing) never adds the two.
  • Scenario: A real noisy sofa scan whose marching cubes adds 30 MB on top of a 12.4 MB volume.
    • True peak extra: about 42 MB, which fails the 40 MB criterion.
    • The lab reports max(≈13, 30) = 30 MB, so c3_extra_pss_le_40mb = true.
  • Aggravating factor (debug build, which the spike uses): In ShapeScanPipeline.process, the local val vol (:111) still references the volume after holder.volume = null. A debuggable ART runtime keeps locals live to the end of the method, so the debug run measures the "volume kept to the end" pipeline, not the one release ships.
    • This makes later stages pessimistic, but it doesn't repair the marching-cubes under-count above.
  • Fix:
    • Compute extraProcessing = peakProcessing − processingBaseline + volumeBytes, or report a separate pss_extra_processing_incl_volume_mb.
    • Take the processing baseline only after the AR session's teardown has settled (it is closed asynchronously when the PROCESSING step replaces the AR screen). Otherwise the camera and GL release during processing pushes the deltas down further.
    • Move "noise + marching cubes" into a helper that reads holder.volume itself, so no caller-frame local outlives the release.
    • Add a LabMetricsTest case: baseline including the volume, plus a stage peak, must report extra ≥ the volume.
  • If skipped: criterion 3 can PASS on a phone where D would actually exceed the 40 MB budget.

MINOR

3. N1: a qualifying point-only bin below the real floor still beats a plane-backed floor: ar/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/ar/FloorEstimator.kt:94-110.

  • Problem: estimate() returns the lowest qualifying bin. A bin qualifies through one plane hit, or through ≥ 5 point hits spread over ≥ 15 cm. A plane-backed floor bin gets no priority over a point-only bin below it.

  • Scenario: On a glossy vitrified floor, the reflected top edge of a 45 cm TV unit is a horizontal line of mirrored features. Sweeping the reticle across it can give ≥ 5 point hits with an estimated horizontal normal, spread over more than 15 cm, in one 2 cm bin at −0.45 m.

    • That bin becomes "the floor".
    • Every genuine wall–floor tap is then rejected (more than 3 cm off the floor).
    • The wall centre-height readout reads 45 cm high.

    The new test covers only a single-spot reflection. Whether reflections give horizontal-normal point hits at all is a device question (TESTING §18 item 4).

  • Fix: Use the lowest plane-backed bin whenever one exists. Fall back to point-only bins only when no bin has a plane vote. Add a test with a spread point-only cluster 45 cm below a plane floor.

4. Template immutability is a convention only, with no test guarding shipped geometry: engine/src/main/kotlin/com/spaceview/engine/furniture/FurnitureTemplate.kt:118-124; shared constants CUSHION_GAP (SofaTemplates.kt:189), Board.* (CabinetTemplates.kt:16), SofaParams.LEG_SIZE/MIN_SEAT_W, cornerLegs.

  • Problem: The KDoc says "never change the geometry of a shipped id". The determinism tests compare two builds within one run. Nothing pins sofa_v1 (or any other id) across commits, and several constants are shared between templates.
  • Scenario:
    • A look change: a later tweak to CUSHION_GAP for a new sofa_v2 silently changes every stored sofa_v1/lsofa_v1 the next time a glbVersion bump regenerates them. No test fails.
    • A range change: tightening MIN_SEAT_W makes some stored rows invalid. partsOrNull then returns null, and the user's saved sofa shows as a plain box.
  • Fix: Add a golden test per template id: for fixed parameter maps (the defaults, each preset, and one boundary map), assert a SHA-256 of GlbWriter.writeParts(build(p)) and that validate stays empty. The test's message should say "ship a new _vN instead".

5. Thermal SEVERE at capture start gives a 90 s dead capture: LabViewModel.kt:197-199.

  • Problem: thermal.start() immediately forwards the current status to capture.onThermal() before c.start(vol).
    • At SEVERE, governor.stopped becomes true, but stop() is a no-op because the capture isn't running yet.
    • start() then sets running = true, and governor.due() stays false for the rest of the run.
  • Scenario: The phone is already SEVERE (a repeat run without cooling). The HUD shows a running capture that integrates nothing until the 90 s TIME_CAP. Processing then reports "no depth frames were integrated".
  • Fix: Call thermal.start() after c.start(vol) succeeds, or make start() return false (or stop at once) when governor.stopped.

6. Two per-run checks don't mean what §7.1.10 says: LabMetrics.kt:217-218.

  • (a) c3_no_severe: On API < 29, ThermalMonitor records −1, so thermalMax = -1 < 3 gives true, a pass with no data.
    • Fix: Null when every status is negative.
  • (b) c2_rate_ge_3hz: It uses the achieved average (framesIntegrated / capture_s). That folds in the blur and view-diversity gates and the seconds before the user starts walking. Criterion 2 is about the governor's integration rate.
    • Scenario: A careful slow walk (the protocol asks for one) with the governor at 5 Hz can still average below 3 integrated frames per second, which reads as a false FAIL.
    • Fix: Also log the time-weighted governor rate, and key c2_rate_ge_3hz on that rate. Append the new columns; don't reorder.

7. Depth intrinsics come from the texture and colour from the CPU image, but neither image's size is logged: DepthCaptureListener.kt:339-345, :438-458.

  • Problem:
    • The intrinsics are textureIntrinsics scaled independently in x and y to the depth size. That is correct only if the depth image covers the texture's field of view.
    • Colour is decimated from the CPU image, whose field of view can differ: selectCameraConfig picks the largest texture with a CPU image ≤ 1280 px, so a 16:9 texture next to a 4:3 CPU image is plausible.
    • The metrics record only depth_w/depth_h.
  • Scenario: On such a config, vertex colours are offset or stretched. If the depth image is 4:3 while the texture is 16:9, the anisotropic sx ≠ sy scaling distorts geometry too. Criterion 1 would then fail, and the spike would blame depth noise, not intrinsics.
  • Fix: Append texture_w/h, cpu_w/h and an aspect_mismatch flag to the CSV and JSON. This is cheap, and it makes a criterion-1 failure diagnosable before anyone concludes "depth is bad".

8. A Back press during the ~100 ms "starting" window leaks the recorders into the next run: LabViewModel.kt:149, 193; LabPerf.kt:27.

  • Problem:
    • backToIntro() detaches, but it doesn't null capture, so if (capture !== c) doesn't catch the abandoned start.
    • c.start(vol) then runs with no session. No frames arrive, so the time cap never fires, and frames, thermal and pssJob keep running.
    • On the next beginAr → startCapture, FrameIntervalRecorder.start() returns early because it is still running and doesn't clear. The new run's ar_frame_ms_* then mixes in the old samples, and two PSS jobs append to the list.
  • Fix: In backToIntro(), set capture = null (or a generation counter) and stop frames, thermal and pssJob.

9. Gate §8 D8 / K2 for D are not exercised. The lab is not the D flow, so this is a note for D integration, not a defect in the harness. The lab's direct save calls neither ads.recordCompletedScan() nor the visit tracker. That is fine, because the lab is debug-only with no ads. When D integrates, the save path must move to GatedGalleryStore (HANDOFF says so) and record the completed scan, and MeasureVisitTrackerTest must gain the D case (gate D7). I'm counting this as a MINOR only so it isn't lost: D integration must not copy the lab's save path.

Nits (not counted)

  • N-a: GlbWriter.kt:436: the KDoc /** Extents (W, H, D) of [pos] without moving it. */ now sits above aabbCentre's KDoc, so it dangles and extents() has none.
  • N-b: AppNavHost startScan (N4): a second Scan tap on the new screen during the ≤ 1 s check is swallowed, because the guard says "active" and the first check then drops its result. The user taps again; no harm.
  • N-c: ARCH §6.2 says "Gallery FAB → Add furniture". The build has the Home row plus the empty-gallery button only, so a non-empty gallery has no furniture entry. This is a spec deviation to note, not a bug.

Gate M4-P1 §8 requirements: were they met?

D (spike harness only, as scoped)

# Requirement Status Evidence

D2 Pipeline order exactly as in ReconMemoryTest Met ShapeScanPipeline.kt: noise and coverage from the volume → marching cubes → holder.volume = null → floor clip max(1 cm, v) → keepLargestComponent(insideBox = local) → decimate → MeshExtent + cross-check → writeMesh(keepInputOrigin = true). This matches ReconMemoryTest line for line. The pipeline decimates to 15k, as D2 says, where the test uses DEFAULT_TARGET_TRIANGLES = 20_000. The caller-local vol caveat is in MAJOR 2.

Walls use the real centre (attachOffset, centreHeight); floor and table use the declared base (declaredCentre). The reserved keys can't be forged (test). phase0.md is updated. Every command (drop, moveWorld, rotate90, twist, clearPlacement, a new anchor pose) invalidates the cache. The camera pose → engine conversion and the Preview state still allocate per frame. HANDOFF's "N5 partial" is accurate.

Harness threading and correctness: checked and clean

  • ARCore objects stay on the session thread (main):
    • Every Session/Frame/Camera/Image call is inside the ArFrameListener callbacks.
    • start/stop/onThermal are @MainThread, called from viewModelScope (Main) or the main executor (thermal listener).
    • The fusion worker touches only the slot and the volume.
  • Image close on every path: depth, confidence and the CPU image are each in use {}. The early returns inside use (repeated, stale, size mismatch, no slot, no confidence) all close the image. The no-confidence path also releases the slot.
  • Slot-reuse race:
    • DepthSlot.busy is @Volatile. The worker clears it only after integrate returns, and main acquires only !busy slots.
    • The channel send gives happens-before for the slot contents. Capacity 2 equals the ring size, so trySend can't fail on capacity, and a failed send releases the slot.
  • Worker join: finish() joins the worker before processing, which gives happens-before for the volume and for fusionNs.
  • Camera pose:
    • It is Camera.getPose() (not the display-oriented pose), and it is read on the frame whose depth timestamp equals frame.timestamp.
    • The conventions match DepthFrame and TsdfVolume: −Z forward, +Y up, rows downward (TsdfVolume.kt:182).
  • Intrinsics: texture intrinsics scaled to the depth resolution (see MINOR 7 for the aspect caveat).
  • Depth source:
    • RAW when RAW_DEPTH_ONLY is supported, under the session's AUTOMATIC mode (raw images are available there).
    • HARDWARE from the active camera config's REQUIRE_AND_USE.
    • Otherwise SMOOTHED, with confidence filled to 255 and sampleWeight from DepthSource.
    • It falls back to SMOOTHED once, after 10 non-NotYetAvailable raw failures before the first success.
  • Timestamps:
    • A repeated frame timestamp returns before touching any state.
    • A stale or repeated depth image is skipped and counted, without consuming the "due" slot, so the next frame retries.
  • Stops:
    • USER, 90 s cap, SEVERE, session pause or recreate (a new world frame), and screen left.
    • SEVERE stops at once, and MODERATE steps down without a cooldown.
    • The rate never steps up.
  • Metrics schema:
    • The CSV columns are a fixed append-only list, and the header is re-checked: a different header rotates the old file.
    • Quoting follows RFC 4180, numbers are formatted with Locale.ROOT, and the JSON has schema: 1 with typed text columns.
    • LabMetricsTest exists (testDebug).
  • Choreographer metric: it measures the UI and AR render cadence that gfxinfo would, with no allocation per frame. p95 ≤ 33 ms matches criterion 2.
  • PSS sampling:
    • Debug.getPss runs on IO, every 1 s during capture and after each processing stage.
    • Sampling at stage boundaries can miss a peak inside a stage, but ART rarely gives heap pages back within a stage, so the reading leans high. The baseline error is MAJOR 2.
  • Lab absent from release (source-level):
    • Lab classes, layouts, strings and the <activity> exist only in app/src/debug and app/src/testDebug.
    • build.gradle.kts has only debug and release build types, with no initWith(debug).
    • The Settings link is behind if (BuildConfig.DEBUG) (constant-folded) and names the activity by string only.
    • main has one string, settings_scan3d_lab, with a Hindi copy; it is harmless in release.
    • The activity is not exported.
    • The share path uses the existing cache/share/ FileProvider root.

Cross-cutting

  • Shared-file merges are correct:
    • AppNavHost: the N4 guard and the furniture destination and entries are both present, and they don't conflict.
    • strings_place.xml: one change, in EN and HI.
    • GalleryRepository: A's centre = info.centre and B's palette regeneration are independent hunks.
    • GalleryDrafts: PlacementModel.centre and the TemplateModelSource.palette() default sit side by side.
  • Hindi parity (script):
    • Every values/strings*.xml in main and debug has the same keys in values-hi. The only exception is the pre-existing untranslatable app_name.
    • The format placeholders match for every key. The script's three hits were regex artefacts (a full stop after %1$s).
  • Room: no entity or schema change, so v3 stands (the amendment window is closed, per HANDOFF).

Risks to the user's spike run (summary)

  1. BLOCKER 1: every run drops to 2 Hz within about 3 s and logs a false FRAME_TIME cause. Fix it before the user captures anything.
  2. MAJOR 2: c3_extra_pss_le_40mb can pass when the true peak fails. Fix it, or at least read pss_peak_processing_mb − pss_processing_baseline_mb + volume_mb by hand.
  3. Debug build (orchestrator decision): pure-Kotlin fusion and marching cubes on a debuggable runtime can be several times slower than release. c2_fusion_le_15ms and c4_processing_le_5s FAIL results on debug are not conclusive; that is what the planned release-signed lab build type is for. The volume also stays live after marching cubes on debug (MAJOR 2), which makes PSS pessimistic.
  4. MINOR 7: if criterion 1 fails, check whether the texture and CPU aspect ratios differ before blaming depth. The current CSV can't show it.
  5. MINORs 5 and 8: they cost runs, not correctness. Start each run cool, and don't press Back while "Starting…" is shown.
